Que. 1 Whether the growth scheme and the transport subsidy scheme which are being 
implemented by the Central Government are in operation as per the prescribed 
targets? 
Que. 8 Out of the 71 Growth Centres proposed to be set up during the Eighth Plan 
period, how many have actually been set up. What are the plans of 
Government in this regard for the Ninth Plan Period? (20th Report) 
Ans: The position as far as the Growth Centre Scheme is concerned is as follows. 
With a view to promoting industrialisation in the country, the Government of 
India in June, 1988 announced the· Growth Centre Scheme under which 71 
Growth Centres (Annexure-!) are proposed to be developed throughout the 
country which would be endowed with basic infrastructural facilities like power, 
water, telecommunication and banking, etc. Each Growth Centre would be 
developed at an estimated project cost of Rs. 25-30 crores in which the share of 
the Government ~f India is limited to Rs. 10 crotes, Rs. 5 crores are to be 
contributed by the\state Government, Rs. 5 crores by the financial institutions 
and Rs. 10 crores a~,required to be raised by the State Government by market 
borrowing. The procedure to approve the Growth Centres requires that sites are 
selected and project reports are prepared by the State Governments. These are 
then apparised by the lead financial agencies, i.e. IDBI, IFCI, and ICICI. The 
project reports are thereafter considered by the Government of India in 
consultation with concerned administrative ministries and approvals accorded. So 
far 54 Growth Centres (Annexure-H) have already been approved for 
implementation of which 13 were approved in 1996-97 alone . .... 
Of the remaining 17 Growth Centres (Annexure-III) project reports in respect of 
4 Growth Centres have been received and these have also been cleared by the 
Project Appraisal Committee during the current year and are being processed 
further for final approval. Project reports in respect of 4 Growth Centres, i.e. 
Sonapur (Assam). Kanglatongbi (Manipur), Majhita (Sikkim) and Ke!:inga 
(Orissa) are yet to be finalised by the State Governments. In respect of Sonapur 
and Kanglatongbi Growth Centres the States of Assam and Manipur respectively 
are considering change of location. In the past too, on several occasions, State 
Governments have proposed change in location of Growth Centres requiring 
preparation of project reports afresh which was a time consuming exercise. The 
State Governments have been reminded at the highest level to expedite the 
finalisation of the project reports. Nine project reports are pending appraisal. The 
financial agencies have also been reminded from time to time to expedite 
appraisal to enable further action Non-participation by the Central financial 
institutions in the Scheme clearly affected the pace of implementation of the 
Scheme in the earlier years. Release of funds by Central Financial Institutions was 
a precondition to grant of Central assistance. A number of meetings were held 
with the central financial institutions. From time to time they were requested to 
release the funds so that implementation could be speeded up. The Central 
Financial Institutions have since inception not released any funds for the Growth

TRANSPORT SUBSIDY SCHEME 
The transport subsidy scheme was introduced by the Government with a view to 
promoting industrialisation in hilly, remote and inaccessible areas. The scheme is applicable 

122 
to all the industrial units (barring plantations, refineries and power generating units) located 
in North-Eastern Region comprising Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, 
Mizoram, Nagaland and Tripura, Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Sikkim, Eight hill 
districts i.e. Almora, Chamoli, Dehradun, Nainital, Pauri Garhwal, Tehri Garhwal, 
Pithoragarh and Uttar Kashi of Uttar Pradesh. Darjeeling district of West Bengal; Andaman 
and Nicobar Islands and Lakshadweep. 
The scheme was introduced by the Government in July, 1971 and has been extended from 
time to time. It was last extended from 1.4.95 to 31.3.2000. 
Under the scheme, subsidy ranging between 50% to 90% is admissible on the transport costs 
incurred on movement of raw material an~ finished goods from the designated Rail Heads/ 
Ports upto location of the industrial units and vice-versa Within the North-Eastern Region, 
subsidy is also permissible on movement of raw material and finished goods from one state 
to another. (Annexure VII) 
The scheme works on disbursement/reimbursement basis, i.e. the subsidy claims are first 
scrutinised and disbursed by the State Government and reimbursement claimed thereafter 
from the Central Government. 
Since the inception of the scheme till 31.3.97, Transport subsidy amounting toRs. 297 crores 
has been released to various States/UTs. Out of these releases of Rs. 297 crores, funds to 
the extent of Rs. 176 crores were released to North-Eastern States, which constitutes 60% of 
total releases made. The details are given in (Annexure VIII). 
As against the original plan allocation of Rs. 20 crores for the Eighth Plan period, an 
amount of Rs. 154.57 crores was actually provided for. The transport subsidy released during 
the period amounts to Rs. 196.44 crores. This was done by obtaining additional funds under 
the scheme. The details of plan allocation and the amount actually released during the 
Eighth plan period are given as under:

Thus in fact higher t1rgets were achieved. 
During the current financial year 1997-98, a budget provision of Rs. 48.30 crores has been 
made under the Transport Subsidy Scheme. Out of the above provision of Rs. 48.30 cr Jres, 
subsidy to the extent of Rs. 25.08 crores has been released to the various State Governments 
· till date. 
For the Ninth Five Year Plan (up to the validity of the scheme i.e. 31.3.2000), a provision of 
Rs. 200 crores has been made by the Planning Commission. Since the Plan Allocation was 

123 
not found adequate for the current year and for the Ninth Plan Period (upto validity of the 
scheme i.e. upto 31.3.2000), the Planning Commission has been requested to enhance the 
plan allocation under the scheme from Rs. 48.30 crores to Rs. 100 crores during the current 
financial year and for the Ninth Plan from the existing approved allocation of Rs. 200 crores 
to Rs. 300 crores.

Que. 7. The action taken by Government on the Committee's recommendation to review 
regularly the criteria for declaration of a State as an industrially backward. 
Ans. In 1968, Planning Commission ~et up two working groups, the uPande Committee" 
to spell out the criteria for identifying industrially backward States/districts and 
"Wanchoo Committee" to look into fiscal and financial concessions necessary for 
promoting industries in backward areas. The reports of the groups were discussed 
by National Development Council and in consultation with, the fiQancial 
institutions, a set of criteria was evolved for identification of industrially backward 
areas in which minimum infrastructure facilities were available. States identified 
245 out of a total of 396 districts as backward districts for the purpose of 
concessions and incentives. 
In 1987 at the instance of Central Board of Direct Taxes, National Institute of 
Public Finance and Policy, NIPFP conducted a study to evaluate the fiscal 
concessions for development of backward areas. The study concluded that while 
the fiscal incentives for backward areas development did successfully promote 
industrial dispersal, the criteiion of identifying backward areas in a State with 
reference to its development indicators rather than all India norms favoured 
developed States. The study, however, suggested enlargement of the s~ope of tax 
incentives for new industrial establishments in Income Tax Act. This was the 
rationale for introduction of full tax holiday for the initial 5 years for the industrial 
units set up in the States/Union Territories specified in Eighth Schedule of the 
Income Tax Act. 
Many representations were subsequently received suggesting that industrially 
backward districts in other States also needed same fiscal support. The Ministry of 
Finance, accordingly constituted a Study Group on Fiscal Incentives for 
Industrialisation under the Chairmanship of Dr. Shankar N. Acharya, Chief 
Economic Adviser, Ministry of Finance. The study group suggested that there was 

138 
need to redesign Central Government tax incentives for backward areas and that 
identification of backward districts in a State for any fiscal incentives should be based 
on objectivity and nationally determined norms and not on norms based on State 
averages. However, the study group did not identify the backward districts which was 
left to another study group constituted in May, 1994 under the Chairmanship of Shri 
M.K. Kaw. This working group was specifically requested to suggest guidelines for 
identifying backward districts and to look into the issue of indicators for determining 
backwardness. The criteria for identifying the extent of backwardness, as suggested by 
the· Study Group on ·Fiscal Incentives, were: 
A. Financial criteria 
- Per capita credit given by sched.uled commercial banks. 
- Per capita deposit received by scheduled commercial banks. 
B. lnfrastructural criteria 
Phones per thousand population 
Per capita power consumption 
Urbanisation 
Metalled roads per 100 square kilometres 
C. Industrial criteria 
- Workers in registered factories per thousand population 
- Per capita gross value added from registered manufacturing 
The Report of the Committee is under consideration of Ministry of Finance and they 
are seized with the matter. Ministry of Industry was associated with these exercises. It 
would, therefore, be observed that the criteria for identification of backward areas has 
continuously been reviewed.

POINT NO. 1 
Whether any cell to monitor the availability of basic infrastructure facilities has been set 
up by the Planning Commission? 
Comments 
Infrastructure projects are reviewecVmonitored in the Planning Commission at the time 
of finalisation of outlays for the concerned sector during the Annual Plan Meetings. 
Presently a Committee of Secretaries in the Cabinet Secretariat is also periodically reviewing 
the performance of the various infrastructure sectors of economy like Power, Railways, 
Shipping, Ports/Roads etc. Ministry of Programme Implementation also regularly monitor 
the status of the various on-going infrastructure projects. 
There is no cell as such for monitoring the availability of infrastructural facilities in the 
Planning Commission. 
POINT NO. 2 
The Action taken on the Committee's recommendations regarding coordination of 
activities of the concerned agencies in Planning. 
The Five Year as well as Annual Plans are formulated, inter alia, based on integrated 
approach and with full involvement of all interests. The Five Year Plans, which are the blue 
prints of development policies, programmes and strategies, are prepared following an 
elaborate process of Working Groups, Steering Committees, meetings at various levels in the 
Planning Commission, etc. At various stages, these involve extensive deliberations and 
discussions with all concerned and interested groups and individuals like different ministries/ 
departments of Government of India, State Governments, leading industrialists of both 
public and private sectors, industry associations, economists, technocrats, etc. 
The draft Plan chapters are also sent to concerned ministries/departments for vetting 
and comments. It would thus be seen that the process of formulation of Plans for each sector 
involves very extensive and detailed consultations with all concerned agencies and 
individuals. 
POINT NO. 3 
Whether any action has been taken by the concerned Ministries on the Committee's 
recommendations regarding development of infrastructure in North-Eastern States? 
Comments 
A number of development programmes have been initiated for the overall 
infrastructural development of North-Eastern Region, Ministry of Home Affairs appointed 
the following Working Groups to assess the infrastructural development requirements of the 
roads and civil aviation sector: 
(i) Working Group on the Perspective Plan for Roads in the North-Eastern region 
(1994). 
Working Group comprising Director-General (Roads), Ministry of Surface Transport 
and other members from Border Roads Organisation, Planning Commission, Ministry of 
Defence and NEC have gone into details of development requirements of National 
140 

141 
Highways, State Highways, Roads under Border Roads Organisation, their expansion and 
maintenance. The Committee recommended financial requirement for on-going and existing 
works at Rs; 11087 crores. The recommendations are being implemented under the various 
schemes of Ministry of Surface Transport and by the State Governments through their Plan 
Schemes. 
(ii) Working Group for the preparation of comprehensive plan for development of Civil 
Aviation in the North-Eastern Sector. 
This Working Group constituted in April, 1995 in the Ministry of Home Affairs has 
identified various airports for development in the NE region. The identified projects will be 
taken up fqr development during the Ninth Plan period. 
(iii) New initiatives announced by the Prime Minister for the development of North­
Eastern Region. 
In the month of October, 1996 Prime Minister announced various developmental 
projects proposed to be undertaken on priority basis for the development of the region. 
Ministry of Home Affairs has identified rail, road and civil aviation projects of the order of 
Rs. 6116 crores which are being taken up on priority basis. 
(iv) Allocation of 10% of outlays out of the overall outlay of the Ministry/Department. 
Under this provision the respective infrastructure Ministries are mandated to allocate 
10% of their outlay for the development of North-Eastern region. 
(v) High Level Commission for tackling backlogs in Basic Minimum Services and 
Infrastructural Needs (Shri S.P. Shukla Commission 1997). 
This Commission has also identified various gaps in the infrastructural development of 
Railways, Roads, Civil Aviation and Inland Water Transport Services. 
POINT NO. 4 
What action has been taken by the Planning Commission on Committee's 
recommendations for setting up of a 'joint decision making body for deciding the aggregate 
sum for the development of Railways in the country's backward region? 
Comments 
The Railway Budget allocates resources for various purposes in the railway sector on 
the basis of operational needs as well as the development demands of various regions. 
Investment proposals are processed in· the Expanded Railway Board which has 
representatives from the Planning Commision, Ministry of Finance (Deptt. of Expenditure) 
and the Department of Programme Implementation. The Board provides a forum for joint 
decision making and gives adequate consideration to the development of infrastructure in the 
country's backward regions.

had to pay import duty. Thereafter, on the finished product, sales tax had also to be paid. 
This problem, they informed the Committee, was not being faced by companies like General

emphasised the need to introduce "Credit Insurance Scheme" and that the Government 
should also stand as a guarantor. The Sub-Committee recommends that the problems of this 
premier undertaking should be solved on priority basis with regard to adjustment in duty 
structure and the· question of allowing the company to participate in bidding including 
financial bidding. Rationalisation of sales-tax may also help the company a lot.

agreed with all the recommendations of the Committee except the observation about the 
abolition of CVD on the imported equipment. Since the observations pertained to the

Export ~tatistics pertaining to performance of small scale sector are collected from the 
various Export Promotion Councils, Commodity Boards etc. It has been experienced that 
besides direct exports of about 34%, SSI Sector also accounts for 6 to 7% as indirect 
exports. There is no specific study about the estimation of such share of indirect exports.

However, the above estimate is based mainly on the following factors: 
(i) A large number of Ancillary units are working in the small scale sector. Such 
Ancillary units supply their products in the form of parts, assemblies etc. to the 
large scale sector. The items under reference are ultimately exported by the 
firms from the large scale sector. 
(ii) A large number of units in the small scale sector are supplying many items to 
the export houses, trading houses in the large sector. These SSI units due to one 
reason or the other are not in a position to directly exports their merchandise. 
These supplies of items, manufactured in the small scale sector to the Export 
Houseslfrading houses, etc. are exported in the world market. 
(iii) Export data concerning export performance of small scale sector is compiled on 
the basis of information received from various Export Promotion Councils/ 
Commodity Boards. These EPCs/Commodity Boards in turn collect export 
figures from their member exporters. But it has been observed that many small 
scale units/exporters do not get themselves registered with the concerned EPCsl 
Commodity Boards. So the export performance of such unregistered units is not 
reflected in the export performance figures compiled by the said Councils/ 
Commodity Boards. But the fact remains that exports from such unregistered 
units take place and form a part of performance of small scale sectur. 
In view of above factors, it is estimated that indirect export from the small scale sector 
accounts for about 6 to 7% of India's total exports. Hence total share of small scale industry 
in the country's exports comes out to be over 40%.

nd  September, 2014 considered and adopted the

REPORT 
 
The Action Taken Report of the Committee deals with  the Action Taken by the Ministry of 
Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises on the recommendations contained in the Committee’s Two 
Hundred Fifty First Report on implementation of Pri me Minister’s Employment Generation 
Programme (PMEGP)  pertaining to the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises. 
 
2.  Action Taken Notes have been received from the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium 
Enterprises in respect of the recommendations conta ined in the Report. These have been 
categorized as follows:  
 
Chapter –I   The recommendations/observations, which have bee n accepted by the Ministry. 
 
 The Committee is pleased to observe that the Minis try has accepted its recommendations as 
mentioned in the Chapter – I of the Report. 
 
Chapter -II   The recommendations/observations which the Commit tee does not desire to pursue 
in view of the Government's replies. 
 
 In respect of these recommendations the Committee is convinced with the logic and 
explanations advanced by the Ministry and therefore do not want to pursue them for the present. 
 
Chapter -III    The recommendations/observations in respect of w hich the Committee has either 
not accepted replies of the Ministry or has asked the Ministry to review its reply. 
 
 The Committee expresses its concern over the non-i mplementation of recommendations 
contained in Chapter – III and desires that the Min istry should furnish logical explanations 
therefor. 
 
Chapter -IV    The recommendations/observations in respect of wh ich final replies of the Ministry 
have not been received. 
 
 In respect of recommendations placed in Chapter-IV , the Ministry has either furnished the 
interim replies or couched its language in vague te rms like noted for compliance/guidance, 
therefore, the Committee desires that the Ministry should furnish Action Taken Notes in respects 
of recommendations categorized in Chapter-IV in det ail and to the point, as per the intention and 
spirit of the recommendations of the Committee. 
 
3. The details of the ATR are being discussed in the succeeding pages. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

-2- 
 
CHAPTER-I 
 
Recommendations/observations, which have been accepted by the Ministry  
       
 
Recommendation/observation 
 
 
The Committee recommends that similar linkages should be established with North Eastern 
Development Financial Corporation (NEDFIC), propose d Women’s Bank envisaged in Budget 
(2013-14), National Minority Development Finance Co rporation (NMDFC) and other similar 
financial institutions.  
(Para 28) 
 
Action Taken  
 
Convergence have already been initiated with Nation al Scheduled Caste Financial 
Development Corporation. Similar efforts will be ta ken up with other related corporations. 
Department of Financial Services (DFS) agreed with the recommendation of the Committee.  
 
 
Recommendation/observation 
 
 
The Committee accordingly suggests that PMEGP proje cts should be developed as clusters 
with common facilities like training, finance and market. 
(Para 31) 
 
Action Taken  
 
The suggestion is welcome. The Ministry has already  initiated a process for development 
of large number clusters of traditional industries under Khadi, Village Industries and Coir by 
revamping the existing SFURTI scheme.  
 
Recommendation/observation  
 
The Committee strongly recommends that the KVIC sho uld give wide publicity to PMEGP 
Scheme, jointly with Banks.  It must be done across  the country and in target areas among 
potential target groups.  The Committee recommends that the banks must publicize PMEGP as a 
bankable scheme.  The Committee appreciates that th e KVIC has developed an exclusive web-
portal to showcase and promote the product range of  PMEGP units.  This will project PMEGP 
products to domestic and international markets. The  Committee recommends that possibility 
should be explored for promotion of PMEGP products internationally as a single Brand name.  
 
(Para 33) 
 
 
 

-3- 
 
Action Taken 
 
 
The suggestion is welcome and the KVIC will approac h Banks for publicity, in addition to 
its existing initiatives.   Promoting PMEGP product s under a single brand name will be explored 
with the proposed marketing organization being set up under PPP.  
 
 
Recommendation/observation 
 
 
The Committee therefore recommends that the negative list should be reviewed considering 
the specific requirements of States, particularly t he North Eastern Region.  The Committee also 
recommends that the Government should enhance the p resence of KVIC in that region and should 
undertake a special drive for the financial inclusi on of the region by expanding banking network.  
The Committee noted that North Eastern Development Financial Corporation has implemented 
Micro Finance Scheme for the entrepreneurs.  The Co mmittee suggests that the KVIC and 
NEDFIC should complement their efforts in expanding  the PMEGP in North Eastern Region.  The 
Committee also suggests that Ministry should develo p PMEGP clusters in NE region under the 
cluster development programme.  These clusters shou ld have financial, marketing and training 
facilities. 
 
(Para 35) 
 
Action Taken  
 
The suggestion is welcome and tie-up with North Eas tern Development Financial 
Corporation will be explored by KVIC for north east ern region. CNG autorickshaws have been 
allowed under PMEGP in North Eastern states on the ground of encouraging micro-enterprises in 
service sector besides encouraging manufacturing/pr oduction activities. Business/trading activities 
in the form of sales outlets have also been allowed under PMEGP in North Eastern states.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
-4- 
 
CHAPTER-II  
 
Recommendations/Observations which the Committee do es not desire to pursue in view of 
the Government’s replies  
 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
 
The Committee finds that the structure of the schem e is too complex. The stakeholder like 
KVIC, DLTFC and Bankers do not coordinate seamlessl y.  The Committee is of the view that for 
efficient implementation of such an important schem e the structure of the scheme must be 
simplified.  The Committee proposes that along with  existing system of extending margin money 
to the entrepreneur an interest subvention scheme m ay also be considered for encouraging the 
youth to become self-employed. 
(Para 5) 
Action Taken  
 
 District level Task Force Committee (DLTFC) headed  by District Magistrates/Collectors is 
a forum for identification of beneficiaries. Implem enting Agencies and Bankers are duly 
represented in DLTFC. KVIC, the national nodal agen cy for PMEGP has taken up the matter with 
all the District Collectors in the country to ensur e that DLTFCs meet regularly. To simplify the 
process of applying for  PMEGP, beneficiaries have been given the option to file applications 
‘ONLINE’ Ministry has also recently constituted a D istrict Level Advisory Committee for 
monitoring the progress of PMEGP at district level with active involvement of the Hon’ble 
Member of Parliament(MP) of the district.  This bro ught to the notice of the Committee that the 
Margin Money under this scheme will be released to the Financial branch from KVIC and the 
same will be kept in the form of FDR’s in the name of the entrepreneur & no interest will be 
charged on the equivalent amount of the loan(disbur sed) for a period of 3 years after which it will 
be adjusted to the loan account of the entrepreneur.      
 As regards considering interest subvention under P MEGP scheme, the issue will be 
appropriately considered at the time when the scheme is revised next. 
 
Further Recommendation/observation 
 
 
In this respect the Committee takes note of the submission made by the Secretary, D/o 
Financial Services, during its meeting on 15 th  April, 2014. Elaborating on the issue of interest 
rates, he stated that “it depends on the cost of fu nds. It is regulated by the RBI. We will have 
to talk to RBI. I don’t have any immediate solution  to this because it is a complex issue. “ To 
a query pertaining differential approach to this pr iority sector as agriculture, the Secretary 
further responded” Sir, there is no differential ap proach. The Government has to provide 
subventions. “ To another related query if it was n ecessary to have differential approach,  
and if there were some concrete proposals, the Secr etary admitted that “ this issue has to be 
addressed at higher level. What sector are to be provided, what subvention has to be decided, 
we will put these before the right level.”As regard  involving Hon’ble MPs in the DLTFCs, 
Members from both Houses i.e. Lok Sabha as well as Rajya Sabha, should be involved. 

 
-5- 
 
In view of submission made by the Secretary, D/o Fi nancial Services, the Committee 
proposes to pursue the issue in future. 
 
 The Committee recommends that Ministry must study the similar scheme being 
implemented by State Government of Goa with  intere st subvention and on  more liberal 
terms.  As a result the performance of State Govern ments Schemes has been much better 
than the PMEGP in that State. 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
 
The Committee is of the view that manufacturing sector has greater employment potential, 
therefore it should have larger share under the scheme. 
(Para 14) 
 
Action Taken  
 
The share of manufacturing sector in project assist ed under PMEGP is indicated in the 
following table.  
 
Year Manufacturing Sector Service sector 
2009-10 70.44% 29.56% 
2010-11 67.57% 32,43% 
2011-12 63.16% 36.84% 
 
Efforts would be made by KVIC to encourage more man ufacturing units to come up under 
PMEGP in future.  
 
 
Further Recommendation/observation  
 
 The Committee observes gradual reduction over the years, in share of manufacturing 
sector under PMEGP. 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
 
However the Committee is of the opinion that such s tate of affairs cannot be attributed to 
Banks alone.  There has to be regular meetings of D istrict Level Task Force as per the prescribed 
guidelines.  Also the DLTFC should do due diligence  while examining a proposal, so that they 
recommend only sound and viable projects and least time is wasted by the Banks in further 
scrutinizing the applications.  The KVIC and RBI sh ould formulate templates against which the 
DLTFC should examine a proposal.  Still, the Commit tee finds prevailing state of affairs grossly 
unsatisfactory, where the KVIC has admitted that th e number of applications exceed the annual 
target and yet they are not disposed off within a f inancial year and instead, the money allocated 
remains idle with the Banks.  And yet, the KVIC cla ims to have met the target.  The Committee 
recognizes that PMEGP has great potential for remunerative self employment by imparting skill.   

 
-6- 
 
The scheme will enable urban and rural unemployed y outh to use their skills for earning their 
livelihood.  The Committee has therefore always sup ported enhanced allocation for the PMEGP.  
There is however need for greater and effective mon itoring by the KVIC, RBI, State Governments 
and Ministry of Finance. 
(Para 21) 
 
Action Taken 
 
 
District Collectors and Principal Secretaries, Stat e Governments have been requested for 
timely conducting of DLTFC meetings. Directions hav e been issued to complete all DLTFCs and 
forward applications by September, 2013 during the current financial year. The same is being 
monitored by the State Level Monitoring Committees. 
 
 
The Ministry of MSME has provided enhanced allocati on of Rs.1418.28 crore which is 
34% more than the actual of the previous year. However in view of the large number of application 
being received, there is need for enhancement of the allocation under PMEGP. 
 
       For greater coordination, Zonal Review Meeti ngs are being undertaken by KVIC with KVIB, 
DIC and Banks for monitoring implementation of PMEG P in addition to the meetings of SLMC 
and SLBC in the State. 
 
According to the Department of Financial Services ( DFS), the targets and  achievements is 
monitored at the Zonal, State and District levels b y the Dy. CEOs, Directors of KVIC and the 
Commissioner/Secretary of Industries (DIC) of the S tates Concerned as per the guidelines of 
PMEGP. The issues related to funds remaining idle w ith the banks, may be taken up by KVIC in 
the State Level  Bankers` Committee(SLBC) meetings. In fact, when an issue relating to settlement 
of margin money claims had been brought to RBI noti ce in the past, RBI has advised KVIC that 
meetings of SLBC are convened  every quarter by the  respective SLBC convener banks. The 
members of the Committee include officials from ban ks, RBI, NABARD, SIDBI and senior 
officials of the State and Central Government inclu ding KVIC. These Committees aim to review  
and monitor banking developments in the state  perf ormance under ACP and Government 
sponsored programmes, flow of credit to priority sector, MSME Sector, performance of SHGs, etc.  
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
 
The Committee was dismayed to note that in certain States like Tamil Nadu and West 
Bengal, no fresh applications were entertained for a year, in order to clear the backlog of 
applications pending from previous years.  Such ins tances constitutes the violation of mandate and 
intent of this scheme.  The committee feels that there should not be any embargo on submitting the 
applications, which should be accepted throughout t he year.  The DLTFC should regularly meet at 
least once in two months to examine and approve the cases.  The objective should be to expand the 
coverage of this Schemes and intent of this Scheme must not be diluted due to procedural nuances. 
 
(Para 22) 

 
-7- 
 
Action Taken  
 
No ban on entertaining fresh applications under PME GP was imposed by the Ministry.  
However, commitment in excess to the available budg etary resources is not a desirable situation, 
and might put the beneficiaries in unnecessary hard ship/uncertainty.  Hence, KVIC was asked to 
ensure proper financial discipline keeping in view the budget aspect.  Even then, during 2012-13, 
Tamil Nadu was given Margin Money subsidy of Rs. 60 .84 crore against the original allocation of 
Rs. 35.84 crore to meet pending Margin Money claims  arising out of its excess commitment under 
the Scheme after re-distributing the amounts available against slow-performing states. 
 
CEO, KVIC has written to all the District Collector s in the country requesting them to convene 
DLTFC meetings regularly and to dispose off the app lications received within 30 days of its 
receipt at their end.  
 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
 
The Committee agrees that there is a scope of scali ng up the PMEGP scheme.  The 
Committee also supports higher allocation for PMEGP in view of the fact that with current level of 
allocation certain States like Tamil Nadu and West Bengal are not able to cater to growing number 
of applications.  However, the structure of the Scheme is too complex and needs to be streamlined.  
The figures and pattern of expenditure suggest that  different agencies involved in this scheme do 
not coordinate seamlessly.  The Committee therefore  recommends that there is scope for 
improving the institutional framework by closely in volving the stakeholders and monitoring their 
performance.  
(Para 26) 
Action Taken  
 
Under PMEGP, Government has already released Rs. 45 75.01 crore upto 2012-13 since its 
inception in 2008-09 and an estimated 20.39 lakh pe rsons have already been provided self-
employment and wage employment opportunities throug h 2.22 lakh new micro-enterprises in the 
country set up with a total margin money assistance  of Rs. 4147.95 crore.  XII Plan has an 
allocation of Rs. 8060 crore for PMEGP, which is 70 % higher than the XI Plan allocation.  A total 
of 27.13 lakh employment is proposed to be generate d through 3.39 lakh micro-enterprises during 
XII Plan under PMEGP alone. 
CEO, KVIC has written to all the District Collector s in the country requesting them to 
convene DLTFC meeting regularly and to dispose off the applications received within 30 days of 
its receipt at their end.  
 
 
It has now been decided by the Ministry that one mo re member may be added in the Task 
Force to represent urban local bodies of the Distri ct, such as Municipalities and Nagar Palikas and 
amongst the three representatives from Panchayats a lready provided in the DLTFC, at least one 
among the three Panchayat representatives may be no minated from Scheduled Caste or Scheduled 
Tribe and Woman. The additional representative from urban local bodies as mentioned  above  will  

-8- 
 
be nominated by the Chairman/District Magistrate/De puty Commissioner/ Collector by rotation as 
is being done in the case of three Panchayat representatives.  
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
 
Therefore, the Committee is of the view that the pr ocessing of projects designed KVIC and 
NSIC, should be fast tracked and should be decided favorably.  Therefore Banks must ensure 
filling in the relevant data in the e-tracking syst em relating to bank’s sanction and disbursement.  
Banks should encourage and ensure that applicant mu st be entered in the e-tracking system.  The 
Committee recommends that all the banks should join in e-tracking platform and that banks should 
start receiving application online.  
(Para 27) 
Action Taken  
 
E-tracking of applications under PMEGP has been int roduced by KVIC in the PMEGP 
scheme. It has been decided that to ensure 100% com pliance of e-tracking system, all the 
implementing agencies will forward the PMEGP applic ations to the Banks after entering the 
applications in the e-tracking system. Banks should  accept the applications of PMEGP received 
through e-tracking system. A circular dated 13.06.2013 has been issued by KVIC in this regard. 
 
State Bank of India has already issued guideline to  all its financing branches. Others banks are 
being persuaded for the same. 
 
A letter is being issued by Department of Financial  Services(DFS) to all public Sector 
Banks (PSBs) to take  the Committee’s observations seriously and act accordingly. 
 
 
Further Recommendation/observation 
 
 
 The Committee reiterates that projects designed by  agencies like KVIC or NSIC 
should be fast tracked.  In this respect Rajiv Gand hi Udyami Mitra Yojna could be a useful 
institution. 
 
Recommendation/Observation  
 
The Committee is of firm view that priority sector must not only get easy access to bank 
finance but also terms and conditions and the cost of credit too should affordable.  In this respect 
the Committee found that the rate of interest charg ed by bank was universally high and also the 
banks were charging differential rate of interest.  The committee recommends that the Government 
through RBI should impose a cap on rate of interest  which should in any case be reduced for 
PMEGP.  As stated earlier, Committee also suggests that along with the existing system of 
extending margin money, the entrepreneurs an intere st subvention scheme may also be considered 
for encouraging the youths to become self-employed.   This in Committee’s view would simplify 
the procedure and minimize the discretion of banks in deciding on an application.   In addition, all 
the loan under PMEGP should be automatically covere d under Credit Guarantee Scheme and no 
collateral must be sought from the beneficiary.  The premium for credit guarantee should be borne  

-9- 
 
 
by the KVIC.  The Committee notes that despite the provision that banks would not ask for 
collateral for a certain amount of loan, in practic al they ask for collateral from the beneficiaries.  
The Committee finds this is an unacceptable situati on which must be monitored by the Banks and 
the RBI at the Branch level and represented on the Boards of the Public Sector Banks through their 
officers.  The representatives of the Ministry shou ld monitor the implementation of Government 
Schemes particularly employment generation schemes like PMEGP by Banks. 
 
(Para 29) 
Action Taken  
 
RBI has issued a circular dated 06 May 2010, in whi ch it is mentioned that Banks have 
been mandated not to accept collateral security in case of loans upto Rs. 10 lakh extended to units 
in the micro and small enterprises sector. However units can also avail guarantee cover under the 
scheme of CGT-MSE. 
 
As per  Department of Financial Services(DFS), RBI has deregulated interest rates. Banks 
charge interest with reference to the Base rate.  R egarding  banks taking  collateral , for loans 
which are  mandated to be collateral free as per ou r guidelines, RBI would  request to furnish bank 
specific cases to enable them to take up the matter with the concerned banks. 
 
Further Recommendation/observation 
 
 
 The Committee finds the reply routine and does not  address the concerns raised by it 
in the recommendation.  The committee proposes to p ursue the recommendation in future as 
well. 
However, the Committee takes note of the submission  made by the Secretary, M/o 
MSME during its meeting on 15 th  April, 2014. The Secretary stated :  
“Now, the question primarily was in relation to the  PMEGP because in the PMEGP scheme, it 
is the commercial rate which is being charged from the entrepreneurs. About the interest rates 
being charged from the small scale industry in gene ral, we have taken it up any number from 
the small scale industry in general, we have taken it up any number of times; there are reports 
of various committees including PM’s Task Force whi ch went into the question of the interest 
rate which is being charge, the cost of loans for the small scale industry. Every one tried to raise 
this issue with the Reserve Bank of India and , of course, with the banks themselves through the 
Department of Financial Services. But, to the best of my understanding, they have not agreed to 
it because of the larger context  under the BASIL norms etc.” 
The Secretary further stated that :  
“This is something which our Ministry has always be en advocating as to having some kind of a 
reasonable interest on the cost of credit for the s mall scale industry. But in the PMEGP scheme 
itself, it is provided that loans would be given by  banks on existing interest rate. So, there is no 
provision in the scheme for providing a subsidy, in terest-subvention kind of a thing, for those 
who are funded under the PMEGP.” 
In view of above the Committee proposes to pursue the issue further.  
 
 

-10- 
 
 
 
CHAPTER-III  
 
 
Recommendations/Observations in respect of which th e Committee has either not accepted 
the replies of the Ministry or has asked the Ministry to review its replies  
 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
 
The Committee however, observes that the above time -line is seldom adhered to either by 
DLTF or Banks.  The Committee therefore recommends that the KVIC with elaborate process of 
monitoring at every level, must ensure scrupulous adherence to the time schedule.  The Committee 
also recognizes that the guidelines provide for mee ting of district level task force every two 
months.  The Committee recommends this should be a mandatory provision instead of being a 
mere guideline.  In addition, the KVIC in consultat ion with RBI should prescribe norms against 
which any application is scrutinized by the DLTFC. 
(Para 24) 
Action Taken  
 
Directions have already been issued for regular con vening of DLTFC meetings.  KVIC 
issued a letter dated 28 th  May,2013 to all CMDs of Public sector banks reques ting to set a time 
limit of maximum 30 days for sanctioning of PMEGP l oan by banks and another 30 days for 
disbursement of loans so that the entire process of  setting up of the project may be not more than 
100 days from the date of receipt of applications f rom the beneficiary.  It is also insisted to ensure  
that complete disbursement of the cases sanctioned is made in a time-bound manner to ensure that 
viability of the projects is not jeopardized.  
 
As per the Department of Financial Services, lendin g is commercial decision which banks 
take on the basis of viability of the project. Bank s have been given  freedom to frame their own 
board approved policies based on their commercial j udgment. Further the banks  representatives 
are also members of the Task Force and as such may take a view. 
 
Further Recommendation/observation 
 
 
 The Committee would like to know the impact of dir ectives by Ministry of MSME 
regarding regular meetings of DLTFC.  The Committee  also takes cognizance of KVIC’s 
letter to CMDs regarding time bound sanctioning if cases under PMEGP.  However, the 
responses of Department of Financial Services puts areas of Banks for its commercial 
viability and their policies.  As such there is no coordination between Ministry of MSME and 
Department of Financial Services. 
 
 
 
 

-11- 
 
Recommendation/Observation  
 
The Committee notes that the schemes were applicable for both rural as well as urban areas 
and suggests that KVIC should conduct a study on th e rural and urban spread of the scheme.  The 
Committee is of the view that the self employment o pportunities in rural areas should be 
emphasized.  In this respect of the Committee takes  note of the recent study done by Institute of 
Applied Manpower Research on informalization of lab our force which suggest that unskilled and 
semi-skilled manpower from villages is migrating to  bigger cities and is being absorbed as casual 
laborers without much social security cover.  Simil arly the recent figures released by NSO 
(National Statistical Organization) indicate massiv e loss and low wages for rural women.  In such 
a situation implementation of schemes like PMEGP in  rural areas will hugely benefit people in 
rural areas and successfully addressed poverty and unemployment situation in our villages.  
However, the Committee notes that the negative list prescribed under the scheme includes industry 
and business connect with cultivation, sericulture,  horticulture, floriculture etc.   Therefore such a  
negative seriously constricts the options of villag e entrepreneurs.  The Committee therefore 
recommends that negative list should be reviewed in  the context of village /rural industry and in 
the context of region.  For instance in the context  of States of north eastern region the negative lis t 
must be prepared taking into account specificities of the States of region.  The respective State 
Governments too should be consulted while preparing State specific negative list.  
 
(Para 30) 
Action Taken  
 
Schemes relating to promotion of Cultivation, Sericulture, Horticulture and Floriculture etc. 
which comes under farm sector are implemented by co ncerned departments. To avoid duplication 
of subsidy, KVIC is dealing with only non farm sector.  
 
As regards negative list, keeping in view of the et hos of Gandhian philosophy KVIC has 
circulated a negative list, which could be duly considered for revision while revising the scheme. 
 
 
Further Recommendation/observation  
 
 The Committee reiterates that there is a need to e xpand the base for which it will have 
to address the local needs and skills.  Also, Minis try of MSME has not responded to the 
Committee’s observation regarding need for a study of rural –urban spread of PMEGP. 
PMEGP must include vocation allied to agriculture i n rural areas and can synergise with 
schemes implemented by concerned Departments. In th is respect the Ministry should study 
the model of similar scheme being implemented by th e State Government of Goa, which has 
performed better than the PMEGP in the State. 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
 
The committee has been informed of proposal for eng aging an agency for concurrent 
monitoring and evaluation of PMEGP.  The Committee expects that the observations and 
recommendations contained in this Report will constitute important references for such evaluation. 
(Para 36) 

-12- 
 
Action Taken 
 
 
The evaluation agency has already been selected and the report is expected in due course.  
 
Further Recommendation/observation 
 
 
 The Committee finds the reply generic and evasive.  The Committee therefore is of 
opinion that the Ministry should recommend the Scheme for comprehensive performance 
audit by the CAG.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

-13- 
 
 
CHAPTER-IV 
 
 
 
Recommendations/Observations in respect of which fi nal replies of the Ministry have not 
been received 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
 
The Committee also notes that there is a prominent training component built in the PMEGP 
scheme.  The training institutions should be spread  all over the State.  The selection of training 
institutions should be transparent under standard t erms and conditions.  The KVIC should monitor 
the training module and employability of trainees. 
(Para 32) 
Action Taken  
 
The original guidelines for selecting the EDP cente rs with transparent and standard terms 
and conditions have already been circulated by KVIC, which would be considered for modification 
on the receipt of feedback from fields. 
 
Further Recommendation/observation 
 
 
 The Ministry may provide details of new Draft Guid elines and feedback there on, to 
the Committee for its further examination. The Ministry should also inform about the norms 
set  to ensure wider spread of such skill developme nt centers. It is also imperative that these 
Centers should maintain data on employability of their trainees. 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
 
The Committee also recommends that the scope of the  scheme should be expanded.  So far 
the mandate of this scheme has been to assist the n ew units.  The Government should explore the 
possibility of assisting the existing PMEGP units f or their expansion and for this purpose some 
percentage of the allocation should be earmarked.  
(Para 34) 
Action Taken  
 
The recommendation will be duly considered at the t ime of next round of revision of the 
scheme guidelines for continuation to XII Plan alon g with finding of independent evaluation, 
which is underway.     
 
Further Recommendation/observation  
 
 The Committee may be informed of the outcome of su ch review particularly in 
context of its recommendation. 
 
 

-14- 
 
III                                                  
Third Meeting

REPORT 
 
The Action Taken Report of the Committee deals with  the Action Taken by the Ministry of 
Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises on the recommendations contained in the Committee’s Two 
Hundred Forty Seventh Report on implementation of I nterest Subsidy Eligibility Certificate 
(ISEC) Scheme  pertaining to the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises. 
 
2.  Action Taken Notes have been received from the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium 
Enterprises in respect of the recommendations conta ined in the Report. These have been 
categorized as follows:  
 
Chapter –I   The recommendations/observations, which have bee n accepted by the Ministry. 
 
 The Committee is pleased to observe that the Minis try has accepted its recommendations as 
mentioned in the Chapter – I of the Report. 
 
Chapter -II   The recommendations/observations which the Commit tee does not desire to pursue 
in view of the Government's replies. 
 
 In respect of these recommendations the Committee is convinced with the logic and 
explanations advanced by the Ministry and therefore do not want to pursue them for the present. 
 
Chapter -III    The recommendations/observations in respect of w hich the Committee has either 
not accepted replies of the Ministry or has asked the Ministry to review its reply. 
 
 The Committee expresses its concern over the non-i mplementation of recommendations 
contained in Chapter – III and desires that the Min istry should furnish logical explanations 
therefor. 
 
Chapter -IV    The recommendations/observations in respect of wh ich final replies of the Ministry 
have not been received. 
 
 In respect of recommendations placed in Chapter-IV , the Ministry has either furnished the 
interim replies or couched its language in vague te rms like noted for compliance/guidance, 
therefore, the Committee desires that the Ministry should furnish Action Taken Notes in respects 
of recommendations categorized in Chapter-IV in det ail and to the point, as per the intention and 
spirit of the recommendations of the Committee. 
 
3. The details of the ATR are being discussed in the succeeding pages. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
-2- 
 
CHAPTER-I 
 
Recommendations/observations, which have been accepted by the Ministry  
       
Recommendation/Observation  
 
The Committee observes that the banks have not comp lied with the RBI guidelines in this 
regard which were based on the Kalia Committee's re commendations.  A mechanism must be 
created to monitor the implementation of guidelines .  Any breach of such guidelines must be dealt 
with seriously.   
(Para 9) 
Action Taken  
 
As directed by DRPSCI, KVIC has made all efforts to  familiarize the bankers about the 
scheme and placed the details of the scheme on the KVIC website.  CMDs of all 27 Public Sector 
Banks have also been requested to issue necessary i nstruction to the Bank to ensure that adequate 
finances under ISEC scheme are made available to Khadi Institutions. 
According to Department of Financial Services(DFS),  the recommendations of Kalia 
Committee are very specific to Khadi and Village in dustries whereas Nayak Committee are 
general in nature. Therefore the recommendations of  Kalia Committee and formula suggested by 
them for extension of credit by the banks to SSI/MS ME sector is based on empirical research and 
ground realities of MSME sector. Keeping this in vi ew, the requirements of credit to Khadi 
institutions should be based on the recommendations  of Kalia committee which has already been 
accepted by the RBI.  However, the suggestions of t he banks regarding, associations of the banks 
with khadi institutions at state level and monitori ng of the scheme at state level through SLBC is 
agreed to by this Department.  State offices /Zonal  offices of KVIC should be mandated to have 
periodical and regular interactions with the banks in order to help the khadi societies sufficient 
credit availability from the banks as per their req uirements.  The review of the progress of the 
scheme may be a regular agenda in SLBC meetings and quarterly meeting by KVIC with banks 
 
 
 
 

 
-3- 
 
 
CHAPTER-II  
 
Recommendations/Observations which the Committee do es not desire to pursue in view of 
the Government’s replies  
 
 
Recommendation/Observation  
 
The Committee feels that such conditions of maintai ning a stock of value higher than the 
sanctioned amount, is too stringent a condition which will only make a khadi unit unviable.   
(Para 12) 
Action Taken  
 
KVIC has already directed the field Directors to ta ke-up the issue of the credit requirement 
of Khadi institution in SLBC/DCC. Further, CMDs of all 27 Public Sector Banks have also been 
requested to include banks credit to Khadi Sector under ISEC Scheme as a standing agenda  for the 
meetings of SLDCs/DLBCs and in such other fora and  issue necessary instruction to the Bank to 
ensure that adequate finances under ISEC scheme are made available to Khadi Institutions. 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
 
 
  In this regard the Committee takes note of the su bmission made by the  representative 
of the State Bank of India, during its meeting on t he issue on 15 
th  April, 2014. It was stated 
that issue was essentially of difference in interest subsidy approved by the KVIC and amount 
actually claimed. 
 
 “ The issue, apparently, is that of a difference in t he interest subsidy approved by the KVIC and 
the amount which is, actually, physically claimed b y the bank on that interest subsidy.  In my view, 
what really happens is that the loans are sanctione d based on certain projections made by 
borrowers.  And the interest subsidy sanctioned by the KVIC is based on the projections made, for 
example, for the first year of operation.  But, act ually, we have seen in many cases, what really 
happens is that after the first year is completed, the projections do not really take place 100 per 
cent; I mean, the projections may be 50 per cent or  60 per cent or 70 per cent.  So, 
correspondingly, the amount of drawing on the loan is also 50 per cent or 60 per cent or 70 per 
cent, and the interest applied is also that much le ss.  One of the major reasons, to my mind, for the 
difference is that the actual performance, especial ly, in the first year does not match with the 
projections made at the time of sanctioning the loa n.  The second thing which I would like to 
submit  is that  it will,  perhaps, be  a good  idea to have, in the State-level Banker ’s Committee, a  

 
-4- 
 
Sub Working Group or a Sub Group of Bankers, KVIC a nd local State-Government functionaries, 
just like they do for PMEGP, to decide on the appli cations, a joint appraisal of these applications, 
and forward them to the banks concerned in that area for approval.   “ 
 
The representative of Punjab national Bank, too, supplemented : 
 
“The gap between financing, as suggested by the KVI C, and those sanctioned by the bank happens 
from two counts.  One is the Margin Money which is supposedly taken by the KVIC at not more 
than 10 per cent.  Banks, normally, finance between  10 and 25 per cent of the margin, which 
results in lesser financing to that extent because the borrower ’s contribution is expected to be a 
little more than ten per cent in such cases.  Secon dly, we have also mentioned in the Report that 
the bank does not finance full stocks.  So, because  of the drawing power, in case the borrower has 
a 25 per cent margin, he is supposed to maintain a stock of, say, 1,33,000 for drawing a D.P. of 
Rs. 1 crore, and this is only because of Margin Mon ey.  It would result in that gap. And, as rightly 
suggested, we can standardize the forum and we can monitor closely.  One of the bankers would be 
a part of this Joint Appraisal between the KVIC and the banks.” 
 
 In views of submission made by the representatives  of Banks, the Committee 
apprehends that resolution of bottlenecks in implem entation has been left to SLDCs/DLBCs.  
But these bodies work under overall policy guidelin es of RBI and respective Banks.  The 
Committee is of the view that first there should be  consensus over policy level between KVIC 
and Bankers, before delegating the powers of resolu tion to SLBCs/DLBCs. The Committee 
notes that the KVIC is engaging the CMDs of Banks t o address the issue. Also,  the 
Department of Financial Services are  also abreast with the issue. There is a need to evolve 
consensus among the relevant stakeholders.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
-5- 
 
CHAPTER-III  
 
 
Recommendations/Observations in respect of which th e Committee has either not accepted 
the replies of the Ministry or has asked the Ministry to review its replies  
 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
  
 
The Committee notes that the ISEC is a very good scheme.  However, it regrets to note that 
banks are issuing fifty per cent loans to the total  ISEC issued.  The RBI guidelines based on Kalia 
Committee, governing ISEC mandate that if less than  ninety per cent ISEC issued are honoured by 
banks then the tripartite meeting among the bank, b eneficiary and the State level Director must be 
organized.  The Committee notes with concern that hardly any such tripartite meeting is organized.  
It is a very serious matter.  In the absence of suc h tripartite meeting, the ISEC scheme is not being 
implemented  properly and  effectively.  Such  tripartite  meeting would  provide  opportunities  for 
discussing the problems affecting the khadi institutions and for coordinating the implementation of 
the scheme which involves banks, KVIC and the benef iciaries.  The Committee recommends that 
the KVIC must ensure that such tripartite meetings take place in every State.  Besides, the 
Committee recommends that the State level Directors  of KVIC must also take the initiative to 
organize such tripartite meetings.   
(Para 17) 
 
Action Taken  
   
KVIC has already directed the field Directors to ta ke-up the issue of the credit requirement 
of Khadi Institution in SLBC/DCC.  Further, CMDs of  all 27 Public Sector Banks have also been 
requested to issue necessary instruction to the Ban k to ensure that adequate finances under ISEC 
scheme are made available to Khadi Institutions. DFS agreed with the observations of the Ministry 
of MSME. 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation  
 
The Committee recommends that the KVIC must take st eps beyond writing routine 
letters  with  much  avail.  The  Committee  suggests that KVIC too  should  make  innovative  
 

-6- 
 
modifications to address the concerns of the Banks.  KVIC may even also explore new 
avenues of funding this Scheme  and negotiate with  institutions like SIDBI, NABARD and 
other similar institutions to provide finance to Kh adi institutions under ISEC scheme.  The 
KVIC has also not replied as to why the tripartite negotiation mechanism has not been used, 
in case of disputes.   
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

-7- 
 
CHAPTER-IV  
 
 
Recommendations/Observations in respect of which fi nal replies of the Ministry have not 
been received 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
The Committee observes that working capital amount under the ISEC as approved by the KVIC 
and actual availed credit have increased over the y ears, however, the difference between the two, 
in percentage terms too has increased to about 50%.  The Committee finds such a situation where 
Banks lend only half the amount of credit what is a pproved by the KVIC, patently unacceptable. 
There is a need for serious efforts to bridge this gap. While the Government has formulated 
enabling scheme to address the credit needs of khad i and polyvastra institutions, the policies and 
guidelines for financing institutions are either no t in sync with Government's policy or the 
guidelines are not being enforced by the Banks and the RBI.  The Committee was also informed by 
the KVIC officials that even though the beneficiari es got the interest at the rate of four per cent, 
actually some banks are charging more interest than prescribed.  This is a very serious matter.  The 
Committee recommends that those banks which do so m ust be investigated upon and appropriate 
action may be taken so that such gross breach of banking norms do not take place.  The Committee 
recommends that the banks must give credit to the k hadi institution under the ISEC slightly above 
the base rate.  The Committee recommends that the b anks must honour the ISEC and strict 
instructions be issued to the bank Managers to honour it.  
(Para 7) 
Action Taken  
KVIC has already directed the field Directors to ta ke-up the issue of the credit requirement 
of Khadi Institution in SLBC/DCC.  Further, CMDs of  all 27 Public Sector Banks have also been 
requested to issue necessary instruction to the Ban k to ensure that adequate finances under ISEC 
scheme are made available to Khadi Institutions. 
 
A letter has been issued again by KVIC on 07.04.201 4 to all the CMDs of Banks enclosing 
recommendations of the DRPSCI [under intimation to Institutional Finance Division of Ministry of 
Finance] and Dy. Governor (RBI) seeking their inter vention in the implementation of the 
recommendation of DRPSCI. 
 

-8- 
 
Further, a Committee has been formed by KVIC as per  the direction of Ministry to review 
and monitor the implementation of Guidelines under ISEC scheme at Central level. Monitoring at 
State level will be done by SLBCs. 
 
A committee of Officers was formed by KVIC under ch airmanship of Financial Adviser, 
KVIC to discuss the issue with Western Council of t he Chartered Accounts of India. The meeting 
is proposed to be held shortly. 
 
Department of Financial Services(DFS), Ministry of Finance is also of the view that the 
credit requirements of Khadi Sector needs to be taken by the banks on priority and credit should be  
extended to Khadi institutions based on ISEC issued  by KVIC. As regards the suggestions of 
banks regarding some modifications in the guideline s in the scheme and its monitoring, KVIC has 
already formed a committee and the committee may su bmit its report in time bound manner to 
MSME so that modifications in the scheme may be discussed with the banks and representatives of 
DFS and amendments/modifications, if any be carried out accordingly. 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation  
 
The Ministry of MSME may inform the committee of th e outcome of the said 
Committee. 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
The Committee is aware of the nature of khadi busin ess. Unlike any other business, a 
typical khadi institutions runs an integrated busin ess involving spinning, weaving, wet processing, 
fabric conversion, wholesale distribution and retai ling. Therefore routine banking norms should 
not be applied in the khadi sector.  
(Para 10) 
Action Taken  
There are already guidelines issued by RBI on credi t requirement of Khadi institutions, 
wherein, it was specifically mentioned that KVIC’s assessment may be accepted if it does not 
exceed the assessment made by the banks more than 1 0%. In case the KVIC’s assessment of 
working capital exceeds more that 10%, the quantum of working capital may be arrived at by 
mutual dialogue between the institutions/KVIC and f inancing bank. DFS has conveyed its 
agreement with the observations of the Ministry of MSME. 
 

-9- 
Further Recommendation/Observation  
 
 The Committee would like to know if the mechanism of Tripartite Negotiations in 
case of disputes, has been resorted to, by the KVIC. In context of presentation made before it 
by the Department of Financial Services and represe ntatives of Banks, the Committee would 
like to review the performance of SLBCs in respect of ISEC disbursals.  
 The Committee takes note of the presentation made by the Secretary, M/o MSME, during its 
meeting on the issue on 15 th  April, 2014. The Secretary summarized the issue and stated : 
 
“the peculiar business cycle of the Khadi instituti on which needs to be recognised by the banks 
and once recognised it will lead to an agreed, adeq uate amount of working capital.  If the working 
capital is inadequate, the Khadi institutions will function in a very sub-optimal way, which is also 
happening at many places. We are not able to access  the loans.  This puts their sustainability into 
question and leads to a very vicious cycle in which  their further capability of raising loans and 
repaying loans is affected.  I think as the Committ ee has highlighted, the peculiar cycle of the 
Khadi institutions needs to be understood.  At the highest level, this agreement had actually taken 
place between the KVIC and the banks as to what wou ld be the requirement of working capital.  
But, in practice, the amount of working capital whi ch is being made available is less.  Over a 
period of time, because the working capital is less  even the margin money which is being provided 
for as per the budgetary exercise has also remained  stagnant.  So I think for breaking this vicious 
cycle we need to once again focus on the peculiarit y of the business cycle of the KVIC and the 
engagement between the KVIC and the RBI and the ban king institutions should be revived in a 
more meaningful way.” 
 
In this regard, the Committee recognizes that the G overnment has replaced the 
Seasonal rebate Scheme with Marketing Development A ssistance (MDA), to facilitate the 
Khadi institutions to sell their products year long  instead of during seasonal rebate period. 
The Committee believes that the MDA scheme should h ave reduced the business cycle to 
make it more compatible with Banking norms.   
 
Recommendation/Observation  
 
The Committee concurs with the suggestions emerging  from the study.   The Committee 
particularly recommends that there was a need that the banking institutions appreciate the business 
cycle of khadi sector and the constraints faced by it.  There is a need for alignment of 
banking/financial norms with business cycle of khadi sector. 
(Para 14) 
 

-10- 
 
 
Action Taken 
 
 
There are already guidelines issued by RBI on credi t requirement of Khadi institutions, 
wherein, it was specifically mentioned that KVIC’s assessment may be accepted if it does not 
exceed the assessment made by the banks more than 1 0%. In case the KVIC’s assessment of 
working capital exceeds more that 10%, the quantum of working capital may be arrived at by 
mutual dialogue between the institutions/KVIC and finasncing bank. 
According to DFS, the sales of khadi are discount b ased/ rebate based/season based and 
festivals specific.  Accordingly, the production of  khadi is undertaken by the institutions.  
Moreover, this is a highly decentralized activity a s spinning, weaving, dying, printing, conversion 
into fabrics takes place at different places and th erefore, khadi completes only one business cycle 
in a year. As per recommendations of Standing Commi ttee, banks should not insist on maintaining 
higher stocks by the khadi institutions. DFS has so ught details of non-compliance so that 
consolidated instructions could be issued to all th e banks to agree the present business cycle for 
khadi based on the ISEC issued by KVIC.   
 
Further Recommendation/Observation  
 
The Committee may be apprised of the new consolidat ed instructions to be issued by 
Department of Financial Services. 
 
Recommendation/Observation 
 
 
The Committee is inclined to accept the observation s made by the Chief  Advisor ( Cost). 
Still, the Committee hopes that the detailed norms should facilitate the KVI institutions to access 
the institutional finance at affordable rate. The C ommittee also observes that while the 
Government and RBI has put the sector under priority sector category, yet the terms and conditions 
are too stringent and defeat the entire purpose of placing them in the priority sector. The purpose 
of 'priority sector' is not merely to provide great er access to institutional credit, rather to provid e 
greater access to it at affordable terms.  While financing Khadi, the Banks should not look at it as a 
commodity, they should also look at the noble legacy and philosophy which sustain it. Howsoever  
 

-11- 
 
intangible it may be, Khadi remains a proud heritag e of freedom struggle invoking the ideals for 
which Mahatma Gandhi lived and sacrificed his life. 
(Para 16) 
Action Taken 
 
 
The study of Working capital formula under ISEC was earlier done by Chief Advisor, Cost, 
Ministry of Finance as decided by the Commission ba sed on the recommendation of Task Force 
Committee. The report of Chief Advisor, Cost was pl aced in Commission in its meeting 
March,2013, wherein, the Commission has formed a Re view Committee to study the issue for 
taking suitable decision. The observation and recom mendation of Review Committee was 
discussed in the Commission in its meeting held in June’ 2013 and thereby it was directed that 
detailed proposal acceptable to the banks regarding  working capital formula may be evolved with 
the help of Chartered Accountants . 
Accordingly, a committee of Officers was formed by KVIC under chairmanship of 
Financial Adviser, KVIC to discuss the issue with W estern Council of the Chartered Accounts of 
India. The meeting is proposed to be held shortly. DFS agreed with the observations of the 
Ministry of MSME. 
 
Further Recommendation/Observation 
 
 
The Committee may be apprised of the outcome of the  new Committee set up by the 
KVIC.  The Committee also recognize that the Department of Financial Services to has  been 
 seeking the inputs from Bankers  on  this  Scheme.   Therefore  it  is  advisable  that  the  
Committee set  up  by  KVIC should be in sync with the Department of Financial Services so 
that the outcome should result in consensus.  The C ommittee set up by KVIC may include 
the Indian Bank Association.

Recommendation/observation 
 
Centaur Hotel, Delhi: 
 
 
 The Committee strongly recommends for substantial allocation of resources made 
available to the Air India for making the units wor king under the HCI more financially 
viable and sound.  The amount so released must be i n addition to Rs.11 crore earmarked

as mentioned in the Chapter – I of the Report.

Evolution and Mandate  
The Government of India established the Ministry of  Small Scale Industries 
and Agro & Rural Industries (SSI & ARI) in October,  1999 as the nodal Ministry 
for formulation of policies and Central sector prog rammes/schemes, their 
implementation and related coordination and for sup plementing the efforts of the 
States/Union Territories for promotion and developm ent of small scale, agro and 
rural industries in the country.  Subsequently, in September, 2001 the Ministry of 
SSI and ARI was bifurcated into two separate Minist ries, namely, Ministry of 
Small Scale Industries and Ministry of Agro and Rur al Industries.  In 2006, 
“Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Ac t (MSMED) 2006” were 
enacted by the Parliament.  Pursuant to this enactm ent, the Ministry of Agro and 
Rural Industries and the Small Scale Industries were merged into a single Ministry, 
namely Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises. 
2. The Committee acknowledges that the Micro, Small  and Medium 
Enterprises (MSMEs) including Khadi and Village/Rural Enterprises, constitute an 
important segment of the Indian economy in terms of  their contribution to 
country's industrial production, exports, employmen t and creation of 
entrepreneurship base.  The Committee noted that th e primary responsibility for 
promotion and development of MSMEs lies with State Government.  However, the 
Government of India has always taken active interes t in supplementing the efforts 
of the State Governments.  The role of the Ministry  of MSME is mainly to assist 
the States in their efforts to promote growth and d evelopment of MSMEs.  In 
addition, the Ministry also attempts to address the  common concerns of these 
enterprises.  

-2- 
3.  Instead of assisting the State Government, the Min istry has devised its 
own Schemes and implements them through State agenc ies like KVIBs and 
DICs.  The Committee finds that though State Govern ments are involved in 
consultative process at apex level, and execution l evel, the Central and State 
agencies do not converge institutionally.  For exam ple in the KVIC act, there 
is no institutional arrangement for coordination be tween KVIC, State 
Directorate and KVIBs to execute KVIC programmes.  The Committee 
observes that with greater emphasis of cooperative federalism and setting up 
of Niti Ayog as consultative forum between Centre a nd State Governments,  
the role of the Ministry may be suitably recast with respect of formulation and 
implementation of the various programmes. 
Composition of the Ministry 
 
4. The formulation and implementation of policies a nd 
programmes/projects/schemes for MSME sector is undertaken by the Ministry with 
the assistance of its attached and autonomous organ izations, namely, Micro, Small 
and Medium Enterprises Development Organization (MS ME-DO) or O/o 
Development Commissioner (MSME), the National Small  Industries Corporation 
Limited (NSIC), the Khadi and Village Industries Co mmission (KVIC), the Coir 
Board and three National Level Entrepreneurship Dev elopment Institutes, viz., 
National Institute for Entrepreneurship and Small B usiness Development 
(NIESBUD), NOIDA (U.P.), National Institute for Mic ro, Small and Medium 
Enterprises (NI-MSME), Hyderabad and the Indian Ins titute of Entrepreneurship 
(IIE), Guwahati.  The Ministry of MSME is having tw o Divisions called Small & 
Medium Enterprises (SME) Division and Agro& Rural I ndustry (ARI) Division.  
The  SME Division  is  allocated  the work, inter –alia, of administration, vigilance  
 

-3- 
and administrative supervision of the National Smal l Industries Corporation 
(NSIC) Ltd., a public sector enterprise and the thr ee autonomous national level 
entrepreneurship development/training organizations .  The Division is also 
responsible for implementation of the schemes relat ing to marketing and export 
promotion.  The ARI Division looks after the admini stration of two statutory 
bodies called the Khadi and Village Industries Comm ission (KVIC), Coir Board 
and Mahatma Gandhi Institute of Rural Industrializa tion (MGIRI).  They are also 
supervising the implementation of the Prime Ministe r’s Employment Generation 
Programme (PMEGP). 
5. The Plan outlay for the Ministry of MSME for 201 5-16 is Rs. 2612.51 crore 
and this gross budgetary support has been allocated  amongst the different wings of 
the Ministry as follows:-

to be incurred on KVIC (Rs.229.09 crore), Coir Boar d (Rs. 26.75 crore), MGIRI 
(Rs. 3.24 crore), Secretariat Service of the Minist ry of Micro, Small and Medium 
Enterprises (Rs. 11.50 crore), the office of Develo pment Commissioner, MSME 
(Rs. 21.86 crore) and the Promotional Services Inst itutions and Programmes (Rs.

Allocation and Utilization 
 
8. In year 2012-13, Rs. 2835 crores was allocated t o the Ministry at BE stage 
which was reduced to Rs. 2541.95 crores at RE stage .  However, actual 
expenditure was Rs. 2229.52 crores, with significan t under-utilization of Planned

2277 crores, which was about Rs. 300 crores lower t han the Revised Estimates.  
Again, there was significant under-utilization of Planned allocation.  
10. In 2014-15 too, the Ministry demanded about Rs.  5695 crores as Planned

13. Reasons for massive reduction in various Scheme s, the Ministry explained 
that the general budget 2014-15 was approved only in the month of July, 2014, and 
thus, the utilization of funds during 2014-15 till December, 2014 remained low. 
Subsequently, the pace of expenditure has picked up  since then.  Besides, the
