disbursement to all sanctioned applications may not be possible by the end of FY. From the stand point of
an entrepreneur applicant, it is an unacceptable situation that legitimate benefit of a policy are denied just
because RE was released in the evening of last day of the Financial Year. The Committee fails to comprehend
the use of such release except that the Government's accounts are technically reconciled though without
achieving the intended objective. In such a scenario, the Ministry by its own admission is not able to
disburse money till the end of FY due to technicalities involved in the Scheme and these have not been
sorted out despite Committee's repeated observations and suggestions. The Committee wonders as to why
further enhancement in allocation be recommended despite huge demand for the Scheme which remains
unmet every year. (Para 162)
Action Taken
During FY 2016-17, more than 4.6 lakh applications have been received out of which 171505 applications
were forwarded to the Banks. Upto 31st March, 2017, Banks have sanctioned 77531 applications involving
MM of `1803.63 crore 52912 projects have been disbursed upto 31st March, 2017 involving MM of
`1280.93 crore Thus, 24619 applications already sanctioned by the Banks are pending for disbursement
involving MM of  `  522.70 crore During the FY 2017-18, the BE allocation for PMEGP MM is
1004.49 crore only, which would not be sufficient for disbursement of pending project and projects sanctioned
during the current year. The position will be reviewed in the middle of the FY and demand for additional
allocation will be processed accordingly.
Further Recommendation/Observation
The Committee fails to understand as to why 24619 sanctioned applications were kept pending
for disbursement despite availability of funds. These had to be carried over to the next financial
year, thereby cutting short the already reduced BE for 2017-18. The Committee recommends that
appropriate steps may be taken by the Ministry to contain the vicious circle of carrying over of the
pending applications to subsequent financial years. The Committee may be informed of the
achievements made in this regard.
Recommendation/Observation
A target of establishing 75 new PMEGP units each with investment of 
` 8-10 lakh was set in each
district of the country. The Committee noted that only 200 districts out of 676 districts of the country could
achieve this target. (Para 163)
Action Taken
In order to have equal distribution of targets and to achieve inclusive growth, a target of minimum of
75 projects have been allocated to all the districts in each State with average MM per project been taken as
` 2.00 lakhs (project cost ` 8-10 lakh). During the FY 2015-16, only 208 districts out of the total 676
districts have achieved the target of 75 projects. Efforts were made to achieve the target of 75 units for each
district, State KVIC, Principal Secretaries of State Government were requested from time to time to monitor
the Scheme. District level advisory committees headed by the Hon'ble MPs of respective district also monitor
the Scheme. However, various other factors including availability of raw material, industrial infrastructure,
skilled manpower etc. also contributes to the establishment of micro units in the districts.

40
Further Recommendation/Observation
The Committee finds it difficult to convince itself of the logic adduced by the Ministry that
PMEGP units could not be set up as per the target due to shortage of raw materials, industrial
infrastructure and skilled manpower, which is contrary to the concept of PMEGP wherein Skill
Development is part of the Scheme based on local raw material. The Committee is therefore, of the
view that setting up of 75 units in each District should be made mandatory and Zonal and State
Heads of KVIC may be advised to comply with the condition.
Recommendation/Observation
The Committee observes that all the States, barring Kerala, have missed the target of setting up 75
PMEGP projects per year per District, significantly. If even 75 Micro Enterprises of ` 10 lakh investment
could not be set up in not more than 200 districts in a year then there is a question mark on the effectiveness
of the scheme like PMEGP . The Committee wonders the efficacy of KVIC, DIC and KVIB institutions in
these States which are responsible for outreach and implementation of the Scheme. The Committee may be
informed about the steps, beyond the usual advisory, that have been taken in respect of these State agencies
for failing to meet even a meager target which was set by the KVIC after taking into account the available
funds, average cost of each PMEGP project and desirability for equal distribution of development. The
committee may be informed if the frequency of meetings held by the Review Committee under the Chairmanship
of local MP and what are the major observations. (Para 166)
Action Taken
With the advent of web based PMEGP, the details of movement of the application, meetings at the level
of DLTFC, uploading of data and movement of sanctions to banks and finally approval process of banks and
communication of sanction to the applicants could be monitored through the portal in a transparent manner.
Review meetings at the level of local MPs have been recommended and Ministry has urged all Hon'ble MPs
to chair such meeting to monitor the progress of PMEGP.
Further Recommendation/Observation
The Committee takes note of the limitations encountered in implementing the Scheme, since
it is being implemented largely through State agencies which are outside the control of KVIC.
However, the Committee recommends that Zonal and State Heads of KVIC be made accountable for
not achieving the recommended target of 75 units in each District.
Recommendation/Observation
The Committee recommends that the Ministry must do a survey of survivability of PMEGP projects
beyond 3 years till they repay the Bank loan. The Ministry must also conduct a Survey of the PMEGP units
that have graduated to Small or Medium units. (Para 169)
Action Taken
PMEGP is a back-ended subsidy scheme, MM subsidy is deposited in the Term Deposit Receipt (TDR)
account in the name of the beneficiary and is adjusted against the Bank loan after three years upon physical
verification of units. 100% physical verification of PMEGP units is compulsory, the verification is done
generally during the third year of the setting up of project. As per the physical verification reports, about

41
80% of the units are found working. No survey has yet been made on the survivability of PMEGP units
neither beyond three years nor to ascertain the PMEGP units that have graduated from Micro to Small/
Medium units.
A provision has also been made in the guidelines that the Nodal offices of concerned agencies viz.
KVIC/KVIB/DIC will visit the units atleast once in every 6 months after their setting-up in order to check
their status and provide necessary guidance/handholding and mentoring. A mandatory joint inspection by the
nodal officers of the implementing agency ( viz. KVIC, KVIB or DIC) and the Financing Bank Branch
officials may also be carried out in scheduled manner after one month, three months and every 6 months.
This would also aid in recovery of the loans and put check on projects becoming NPA.
Further Recommendation/Observation
The Committee feels desirability of having timely a survey of survivability of projects under
PMEGP to keep a check on NPA. During its study visit, the Committee observed that there was a
variation in the figures on NPA under PMEGP provided by Banks, and KVIC, with Banks clearing
NPA under PMEGP to the extent of 70%. Therefore, it is essential to do a survey of survivability of
projects under PMEGP. The survey would also facilitate in ascertaining the number of units that
could graduate into Small or Medium units, thus further enabling the implementing agencies to
provide necessary hand-holding to those units that could not graduate into SMEs.
Recommendation/Observation
Having observed the structural complexities in PMEGP that have denied lull and timely utilization of
allocated Funds and keeping in view that average cost of a PMEGP project is between 
` 8-10 lakhs as per
Ministry's estimates, which can be covered under the MUDRA loan that is easy to access and with lower rate
of interest, the Committee agrees with Ministry's suggestion that all the projects upto ` 10 lakhs could be
covered by the MUDRA yojna. New and even old expansion projects beyond ` 10 lakh to ` 25 lakhs may be
covered under PMEGP. The Ministry may change the objective and structure of the Scheme accordingly.
(Para 172)
Action Taken
PMEGP is a credit-linked subsidy programme, aimed at generating self-employment opportunities
through establishment of micro-enterprises in the non-farm sector. Margin Money subsidy of 15-35% is
admissible to the beneficiaries belonging to different categories. Micro units having a maximum project cost
of `25 lakh are covered under PMEGP. MUDRA is a different Scheme being implemented by Department of
Finance, which provide loans from `50 thousand to `10 lakh to existing as well as new units. PMEGP is
available for new units only. As most of the applications under PMEGP are for loan below `10 lakh, KVIC
was requested that the details of PMEGP applicants could also be shared with MUDRA so that the applicants
seeking loans upto `10 lakh may opt for Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY). However, as there is no
subsidy under MUDRA Scheme, the prospective entrepreneurs prefer PMEGP scheme and huge number of
applications are received under PMEGP, which restrain the move for changing the objective and structure of
the Scheme.
Further Recommendation/Observation
The Committee understands that the Schemes of PMEGP and MUDRA are different in their
structure and operationability owing to the fact that the former is a Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme

42
while the latter is a loan Scheme. Further, while PMEGP is administered by Ministry of MSME,
MUDRA is under Department of Financial Services. The Committee takes note of the Ministry's
submission that prospective entrepreneurs prefer PMEGP Scheme due to its subsidy components.
However, it remains a fact that only 1/3 of the applicants got benefits under the Scheme while rest
are rejected for want of funds. Also, it was brought before the Committee that PMEGP loans below
10 lakhs, get reflected under MUDRA. However, there was a difference of opinion in this regard
between Department of Financial Services (SIDBI) and M/o MSME (KVIC).
In view thereof, the Committee is of the opinion that regardless of the Schemes/Programmes
under which assistance is offered, the ultimate aim of the Government should be to benefit the
maximum number of deserving entrepreneurs. Accordingly, the Committee desires that M/o MSME
may co-ordinate with Department of Financial Services and bring about a synergic solution regarding
the overlapping structures between PMEGP and MUDRA, resulting in a possible interoperability of
both the Schemes.
Recommendation/Observation
The Committee may also be apprised if the MPDA claims particularly in respect of artisans, submitted
by the KIs are actually verified by (he KVIC and method of verification adopted. The Committee may be
informed whether there have been cases when Khadi artisans are given work only on monthly, i.e. for a few
months and remain idle for most part of the year. (Para 182)
Action Taken
The MMDA claims of Khadi Institutions (KIs) as well as Khadi artisans are paid by DBT portal specially
designed for this purpose. The MMDA incentives of artisans are directly paid into their Aadhaar seeded bank
account, and their incentives are automatically calculated with reference to their wages earned in the concerned
quarters.
Further Recommendation/Observation
The Committee is of the view that Aadhaar can only ensure that the Bank account actually
belongs to a particular person. The Committee however is interested to know the steps being taken
to ensure that incentives actually go to the genuine artisans.
Recommendation/Observation
The Committee notes with concern very low enrolment under MPDA scheme in the NER. The expenditure
of MPDA earmarked for NER has been negligible every successive year. As per the definition of Khadi in
the Act, the mandate of KVIC is to encourage silk, cotton and/or woolen hand spun and hand woven cloths.
Considering that North Eastern region has rich spun and woven textile tradition, KVIC should not have any
reason for such low penetration of MPDA in that region. The Committee may be informed if the textile
tradition of NE complies with the definition of Khadi under the Act, and why KVIC has not been able to
propagate the MPDA and other Khadi schemes in NE and money under MPDA, KRDP , SFURTI and
ASPIRE remains unspent. In view of such indifferent performance, the KVIC must take a hard look of the
performance of its regional set up and KVIB in these States and inform the Committee of their lackluster
performance. KVIC must encourage and revive the textile tradition in NER through MPDA and S&T schemes.
(Para 188)

43
Action Taken
The MMDA is passed on to KIs based on their actual production during a quarter. The payment of
MMDA to North- East region is comparatively lesser than that of other region mainly due to absence of good
number of KIs in N.E. region.
In all schemes NER is given special treatment and efforts are on to register more KIs under the fold of
KVIC. KVIC is implementing Science and Technology scheme in North East region by allotting 10% of
funds out of its Annual Action Plan every year. Much more efforts will be made to encourage Research
Organizations to undertake R&D projects in NE region.
Further Recommendation/Observation
The Committee is concerned to note the poor performance of KVIC Schemes in NER which
has its own District textile and Craft traditions. The Committee recommends that KVIC must
support Districts spinning and weaving traditions in NER and upscale it.
Recommendation/Observation
The Committee wonders if the objective of the Scheme is to reduce reliance on subsidy, how the Ministry
envisages an increase in MPDA assistance which is essentially a subsidy. The Ministry may elaborate on its
assertion where allocation for both KRDP and MPDA would increase and whether that is the objective of
KRDP . (Para 208)
Action Taken
The MPDA scheme is one of the tranche conditions of KRDP to be implemented in the field in place of
the existing MDA to extend the benefit to Artisans and Karyakartas. The main object of the KRDP is to
extend benefit to Artisans and Karyakartas, besides providing for rationalization of subsidy by phasing out
products which do not need subsidy and doing away with cost chart and bring in the concept of market
linked pricing for khadi products. The quantum of allocation of subsidy under MPDA will not relate to
KRDP allocation. KRDP allocation to meant for to reform the Khadi activities so that KIs will become self-
sustainable.
Further Recommendation/Observation
The Committee takes note that the MPDA has been deviced to cater to one of the tranche
conditions of the KRDP. It is also understood that the KIs can continue to benefit from both the
programmes, which means that KRDP does not intend to eliminate the subsidies currently being
provided under MPDA. However, the Committee feels the need for further clarifications regarding
the simultaneous operations of KRDP and MPDA clearly bringing out the difference in their objectives
and the measures being taken to avoid the overlapping of its purposes.
Recommendation/Observation
The Committee finds above figures suspect. While number of accounts covered under CGTMSE has
increased, the Guarantee amount has come down. The Ministry may elaborate. (Para 225)
Action Taken
The total amount of guarantees depends upon the loan amount and the no. of proposals approved.
However, in general guarantee amount increases with the no. of accounts/proposals.

44
Further Recommendation/Observation
The Committee is of the view that when the Ministry have themselves agreed that when the
number of accounts increases simultaneously the guarantee amount also increase then they may
furnish the reasons for decrease in guarantee amount even though the number of accounts under
CGTMSE have increased.
Recommendation/Observation
The Committee further sought to know if Banks could not claim dues for restructuring accounts from
CGTMSE, then whether any Budget provision has been made for Banks to meet the cost of restructuring and
revival under this Framework for Revival and Rehabilitation. If not, how are Banks supposed to incur the
cost for restructuring loans for MSME units that have been designated as priority sector by Government and
avail bank loans under Government policy. (Para 231)
Action Taken
Ministry of MSME has not made any budget allocation for this Framework. Further, Banks are expected
to bear the expenses for restructuring loans of MSME units.
Further Recommendation/Observation
The Committee reiterates its recommendation that Ministry of MSME may take up with
appropriate authority to enable Banks to claim expenses for restructuring the loans of MSME units.
Recommendation/Observation
The Secretary in his submission agreed and submitted that NBFCs seeking coverage under CGTMSE
has been asked to cap interest rates at 14%. (Para 236)
Action Taken
As per the guidelines of the scheme issued vide circular No. 123/2016-17 dated 25.01.2017, the
NBFCs seeking coverage under CGTMSE have been asked to cap interest rates at 18%.
Further Recommendation/Observation
The Committee is of the view that interest rates levied by NBFCs seeking coverage under
CGTMSE be capped at 14% as has been agreed to by Secretary, M/o MSME. Ministry may take up
the issue at the appropriate level.
Recommendation/Observation
The Committee expresses serious reservations over under-utilisation of funds for such an enabling
Scheme. The Committee is also inclined to accept the view of certain industry associations who suggested
that VDPs should be more substantive in developing the capabilities of MSE vendors instead of merely
providing a Business to Business interface. The Committee also appreciated that after every VDP the
participant CPSEs should be required to enroll at least certain number of MSEs as their Vendors and place
orders. (Para 249)
Action Taken
During the FY 2016-17, the guidelines/norms for conducting Vender Development Programme (VDP)
(NVDPs/SVDPs) was revised. The new sanction order with the revised guidelines and revised targets was

45
released in the month of August, 2016, resulting in low performance till 3rd quarter, thereafter the expenditure
has increased in last. The total 16710 MSMEs benefited through the participation in NVDPs/SVDPs.
Further Recommendation/Observation
The Committee would like to be further informed of the number of CPSEs that participated in
the VDPs that were organized and the number of MSEs, which these CPSEs could enroll as their
vendors.
Recommendation/Observation
The Ministry may share its own databank of MSE vendor and SC/ST vendors with CPSEs or the CPSE
associations like SCOPE so that CPSEs are enabled to locate the relevant MSE vendors, as per their
requirements. (Para 251)
Action Taken
National SC/ST Hub has been launched and NSIC is maintaining the databank pertaining to MSME
(including SC/ST Enterprises) and the details of the same are provided to procuring agencies as and when
they ask for the same.
Further Recommendation/Observation
The details of MSE Vendors including SC/ST Vendors maintained by SC/ST Hubs may be uploaded
on NSIC website so that the information can be accessed by the procuring agencies as and when
needed by diem. Besides, the details may also be shared with CPSE Associations like SCOPE.
Recommendation/Observation
However the Committee noted that the Ministry had not assessed the impact/growth in MSME's
contribution to GDP and employment post - Make in India. The Committee feels that regular monitoring
and survey are essential to measure efficacy of policy interventions and adjustments, if required. The Committee
feels that the Ministry must make a survey to this effect and evolve policy intervention accordingly. In this
respect the Committee asks the Ministry to utilize the Budget allocation for Studies, Research and Surveys.
(Para 263)
Action Taken
The Ministry of MSME has not made any assessment of the impact of Make in India initiative on
MSMEs. Access to finance, availability of timely credit, infrastructure, technology and marketing facilities
are essential for the promotion and development of MSME sector. Ministry of MSME has been taking
various steps for the development of MSME Sector though its schemes and programmes like Credit Guarantee
Fund Scheme, Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme, National Manufacturing Competitiveness Programme (NMCP),
Micro and Small Enterprises- Cluster Development Programme (MSE-CDP), Prime Minister's Employment
Generation Programme (PMEGP), Marketing Development Scheme etc.
Further Recommendation/Observation
The Committee reiterates its recommendation that a survey be made by the Ministry on the
efficacy of 'Make in India' projects, on MSMEs.

46
Recommendation/Observation
The Committee observes that while utilization of funds has increased during last two years, the
achievement in physical target remains tepid. The employability of training Schemes remains serious concern.
(Para 269)

47
Recommendation/Observation
KVIC acts as regulator promoter and certification authority for the Khadi and Village Industry sector.
Its multiple rules may come into conflict. The Committee is particularly concerned about the performance of
State Khadi networks, who are supposed to implement Khadi schemes, and more particularly in the NE
Region. The Committee noted with serious concern that despite rising demand for Khadi, the Khadi institutions
registered with KVIC have shown decline in certain States. Yet, the allocation for MMDA has been increased.
The Ministry remains non-committed about the wages of Khadi artisans. (Para 270)

As for wages of Khadi artisans are concerned, it forms part of factors of production of Khadi. The
wages of artisans are periodically revised with reference to prevailing wages in other sector, demand of
artisans and KIs.
Further Recommendation/Observation
The Ministry by its own submission in reply to Action Taken in respect of Committee's
recommendations at Para 191, has admitted that growth of KIs is stagnant and that efforts are
being made to increase the number of KIs by policy liberalization. Hence even though MDA allocation
has been witnessing increase year after year, there is no corresponding increase in the number of
registered KIs. The Ministry may look into this aspect and report back.

48
CHAPTER-IV
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH THE COMMITTEE DESIRE
FURTHER COMMENTS OF THE MINISTRY
Recommendation/Observation
In view of the size of the MSME sector in the country, a Budget allocation of ` 6482 crore for
Financial Year 2017-18, is just meager and needs to be utilized efficiently and judiciously. (Para 3)
Action Taken
The observation of the Committee is noted. Budgetary allocation of M/o MSME has been increased
from ` 3,464.77 (BE 2016-17) to ` 6,481.96 (BE 2017-18). In order to meet the pending proposal of
CLCSS amounting ` 978.00 crore and to meet increase in corpus Credit Guarantee Scheme from ` 2500.00
crore to ` 7500.00 crore. Allocation of ` 3002.00 crore is made in this scheme for the year 2017-18.
To ensure the efficient utilization of the budget, M/o MSME has been taking following steps:
• Regular review meetings of various schemes under the Chairmanship of Secretary (MSME);
• Regular monitoring of expenditure of various schemes under the Chairmanship of AS & DC
(MSME)/JS (ARI)/JS (SME) on the schemes under their Division.
• Schemes are being monitored as per the provisions laid down under each scheme's guidelines
viz., Screening and Steering Committee (SSC), Project Monitoring and Advisory Committee
(PMAC), etc.
Apart from the above, Hon'ble Minister of MSME and both Hon'ble Minister of State interact with
various stake-holders during regional conclaves, meeting with Hon'ble Ministers/Secretaries of all States/
UTs, meeting of National Board of MSME, etc., for effective implementation of the schemes.
Recommendation/Observation
It was informed that there were about 25.27 lakh MSMEs registered under Udyog Aadhaar Memorandum
(UAM) till 31.1.2017 of which 22 lakh were micro units. The Committee also noted the submission made by
the Secretary of the Ministry that there was no realistic estimation of number and scope of MSMF units in
the country. The Secretary had submitted that the Ministry is in the process of developing an online census
of statistical data of MSMEs. The Committee believes that without realistic and updated information regarding
scope and extent of MSMEs in the country, no worthwhile policy or budgetary intervention can be made.
(Para 4)
Action Taken
A Steering Committee was constituted on Fifth All India Census of MSME. During its third meeting
held on 17th May, 2016, it was decided to discontinue the conduct of Fifth All India Census of MSMEs
because only 10 of the Bids met the Pre-Qualification/Eligibility Criteria. Udyog Aadhaar Memorandum
(UAM) was notified and launched on 18th September, 2015 to enable entrepreneurs to file online simple one
48

49
page form on Self Certification basis to register new units. 30,81,417 MSMEs have registered over the
portal as on the 24th May, 2017.
For facilitating the promotion and development and enhancing the competitiveness of MSMEs, the
Ministry of MSME had notified the MSME Development (Furnishing of Information) Rules, 2016 on
29.07.2016 under which all MSMEs are to furnish information relating to their enterprises online to the
Central Government in the data bank maintained by it at www.msmedatabank.in. 95,839 units have furnished
their information on the portal as on the 24th May, 2017.
This data bank will enable Ministry of MSME to streamline and monitor the schemes and pass on the
benefits directly to MSMEs. It will also provide the real-time information about the status of MSMEs under
various parameters. Data Bank is helpful to MSME units, who can now update their enterprise information
as and when required without visiting any government office and also update information about their
products/services, which can be accessed by government departments to do procurement under Public
Procurement Policy of Government of India.
The process of compilation of Index of Industrial Production (IIP) for MSME sector has been re-
initiated by O/o DC, MSME. The finalization of the parameters like Product basket, frame, base year, etc.
required for the compilation of the index is under progress.
However, Ministry of MSME is reconsidering to conduct Fifth All India Census of MSME, for which
draft approach paper is under preparation while incorporating suitable recommendations of One Man
Committee under the Chairmanship of Shri Prabhat Kumar, Ex-Cabinet Secretary, Government of India and
Ex-Governor, Jharkhand appropriately.
Recommendation/Observation
However, the Committee also noted that ever since 4th Census of MSMEs, the Government has not
conducted the 5
th census which is due. Instead, it has been decided to discontinue the process of census and
look for other sources of collecting reliable data on MSMEs. The Committee feels that Census figures are an
important reference point for any future policy formulation initiative as it provides baseline data to measure
prospective trends. Every year, in DFG, a separate allocation is made to strengthen the database, survey and
research. The Ministry may consider using this allocation for conducting 5th decennial census of MSMEs.
Also, like annual Public Enterprises Survey, Ministry of MSME too should present an annual MSME
Survey on the basis of NSS Rounds. (Para 5)
Action Taken
A One Man Committee had been constituted under the chairmanship of Shri Prabhat Kumar to make
recommendations for National Policy for Small and Medium Enterprises. The recommendations related to
creation of MSME database are given below:
(i) The Committee feels that it is absolutely essential to have a transparent database that can be
gainfully used by the key stakeholders at the national, state and local levels. It is, therefore,
recommended that a task Force should be constituted to give a comprehensive template for the
interactive database within a short time.

50
(ii) The Committee feels that there is urgent need for creating a comprehensive MSME database,
which can be used to deliver a range of services to individual and group of enterprises. These
services may generally be called Business Development services apart from much needed credit
from banks and financial institutions.
(iii) It may be emphasized that the data should not be used for any coercive action against the
entrepreneurs. The database should also have the provision for updating itself.
(iv) We would recommend that the issue of a comprehensive MSME database be considered in
consultation with state government and other subject matter ministries and then placed before the
proposed National Authority at the earliest.
(v) It is proposed that a Task Force be constituted for preparing the scheme of a comprehensive
Database to consider the Committee's suggestions and submit a proposal for MSME INDIA
within a short time. As mentioned in the reply of para 4, the Ministry of MSME is reconsidering
to conduct Fifth All India Census of MSME, for which draft approach paper is under preparation
while incorporating suitable recommendations of One Man Committee under the Chairmanship
of Shri Prabhat Kumar, Ex-Cabinet Secretary, Government of India and Ex-Governor, Jharkhand
for further necessary action in this matter. In due course, the Ministry has launched MSME
Databank in which all MSMEs are to furnish information relating to their enterprises online to the
Central Government at www.msmedatabank.in.
Recommendation/Observation
The Committee feels that an assessment should be made of the impact if any, of demonetisation, on the
credit-worthiness of MSMEs and whether it has led to greater NPAs in MSME sector. The Committee takes
note of demands put forth by certain industry associations that in view of possible adverse impact of
demonetization on the business and overall lack of liquidity in the economy, the time limit for NP A should
be extended from present 90 days to 180 days. The Committee views this demand favourably and recommends
the Ministry to take up the issue with Ministry of Finance and RBI and report to the Committee of its
outcome. (Para 7)
Action Taken
As per RBI's recent study 'Macroeconomic Impact of Demonetisation - A Preliminary Assessment' the
organized sector on a whole remained resilient though some manufacturing and services segments were
adversely affected. Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises had set-up a One-Man Committee
under the Chairmanship of Shri Prabhat Kumar to make recommendations on National Policy for MSMEs.
This Committee has already submitted its report and one of the suggestions recommended by the Committee
is to revise the time limit for NPA. The recommendations of the Committee are under consideration.
No, the Ministry of MSME has not conducted any independent assessment of the impact of
demonetisation on MSME Sector. However, during the phase of Demonetisation, this Ministry held several
meeting with various MSME Associations. The Ministry of Finance was appraised about the same.
Recommendation/Observation
The Committee notes that unlike KVIC and Coir Board, whose allocation is made under ARI Division,
the Office of DC-MSME though has same mandate and implements the same Schemes as SME Division, get

51
separate allocation in the annual Demands. The Committee has been raising the issues of overlapping and
duplication of multiple Schemes of the Ministry. Considering that SME Division and DC-MSME both have
not been able to utilize their allocated funds during previous years, the Committee is inclined to recommend
that two allocations may be merged so that the Schemes are also consolidated with more money available for

Recommendation/Observation
The Committee observed that this Scheme includes the same training, marketing and financial support
programmes whose performance has been indifferent. The Committee noted that under Stand Up India
Scheme out of 1.29 lakh Bank Branches, only some 1000 branches have met their target of lending to one
SC/ST and one woman entrepreneur, fully. Some 11000 branches have met the tar get partially. During the
submission before the Committee one of the industry associations informed the Committee that most of the

Action Taken
The subject matter of credit limit and interest rate on loans under Stand Up India scheme pertains to
Department of Financial Services (DFS), Ministry of Finance. Comments have been sought from them.
Stand Up India scheme caters to promoting entrepreneurship amongst Women, SC & ST category i.e.,
those sections of the population understood to be facing significant hurdles due to lack of advice/mentorship
as well as inadequate and delayed credit. To overcome these hurdles, various steps have been taken by the
Government under Stand Up India scheme which, inter-alia, include provision for online applications through
standup mitra portal, handholding support through agencies which include industry associations, and collateral
free loans etc.
Stand Up India Scheme supports Greenfield enterprises and the entrepreneurs require handholding and
extra efforts of the bank which takes time.
So far (upto 14.05.2017) 2004 branches have met the target lending to at least one SC/ST and one
Woman entrepreneur. 14905 branches have met the target partially. Total loans sanctioned are (SC: 4665,
ST: 1322, Women: 23845) as on 14.05.2017.
The credit limit is between ` 10 lakhs and ` 1 crore. There is also provision for convergence with State
& Central schemes wherever possible. All credit related matters of banks including charging of interest
(ROI) have been deregulated by RBI and are governed by the banks' own lending policies. However the rate
of interest would be lowest applicable rate of the bank for that category (rating category) not to exceed
(base rate (MCLR)+3%+tenor premium).

For facilitating the promotion and development and enhancing the competitiveness of MSMEs, the
Ministry of MSME vide Gazette Notification No. 750(E) dated 29.07.2016 had notified the MSME Development

information about their products/services, which can be accessed by government departments to do
procurement under Public Procurement Policy of Government of India. Special VDPs are being conducted
to bring the PSUs and SC/ST enterprises together at a common platform. The Ministry is writing letter to all
PSUs to nominate nodal officers for handling procurement for SC/ST MSEs.

(NSIC) was instructed to mention the category of MSE while making registration for them. This
is being implemented too by NISC.
• NSIC has conducted Vendor Development Programme especially for SC/ST entrepreneurs in
different parts of the country during the year 2013-14 and 2014-15.

by SC/ST entrepreneurs and for achieving stipulated target of procurement.

Entrepreneurs which help PSUs to their vendor base.

service of more than 100 crore in a financial year, has been requested to conduct V endor
Development Programme including one exclusively for SC/ST entrepreneurs.
Recommendation/Observation
The Committee expresses its concern that the Ministry sets ambitious targets only to be missed significantly.
The Committee had repeatedly cautioned against parallel Government schemes like ASPIRE and Atal

54
Innovation Scheme to incubate entrepreneurship. The Committee's apprehensions seem to be realistic as the
Ministry has admitted that stakeholders find the AIS and Start Up India more favorable than ASPIRE and
are reluctant to avail this Scheme, Therefore there is under achievement of target. (Para 77)
Action Taken
ASPIRE and Atal Innovation Mission (AIM) are two different schemes under the administrative domain
of two different Ministry/Body. While ASPIRE has two components, namely setting up Livelihood Business
Incubator and Technology Business Incubator, AIM plans to set up Innovation Hubs at different locations.
Startup India is another scheme launched under Department of Industrial Policy and Planning (DIPP),
whereby Startups as per scheme definition are supported. Under ASPIRE, Ministry of MSME could approve
50 LBIs and 5 TBIs as on 31.03.2017 and out of 50 LBIs, 24 have commenced incubation related activities.
The concept is new and State Governments are now seeking approval for more LBIs in their respective
States. As far as TBIs are concerned, potential host institutions are gathering pace to propose such facility
in their campuses. In view of this, it may not be appropriate to conclude that stakeholders are reluctant to
avail this scheme. In fact the Scheme Steering Committee while approving 50 proposals has scanned through
at least 80 to 90 odd proposals as of now.

The Committee may be informed about the templates and benchmarks on which the success of ASPIRE
Fund will be judged as the start ups are not funded directly but through Alternative Investment Funds. The

Action Taken
The benchmark of ASPIRE Fund would be largely based on the success in selecting right kind of
Investment Funds and investing the seed money in those ventures. In the case of fund of funds, the funds

55
are routed through specialized institutions that are better suited to do the evaluation. The fund of funds also
provides the same advantage of additional investors who may be interested in pooling in thereby enhancing
the corpus. For a case in point, out of the four AIFs supported under ASPIRE, under three AIFs, 20 investee
companies with a committed investment of `67.45 crore, which suggests that the scope of leveraging the
benefit under Fund of Fund operation is immense.
Recommendation/Observation
The Committee may be informed of the status of 430 new ideas that have been financed under Support
for Entrepreneurship and Managerial Development Programme and details of those who have been
commercialized. The Committee may also be informed if these ideas have been assisted under several innovation
and entrepreneurship development schemes of the Ministry like ASPIRE Fund. The Committee has not been
informed regarding monitoring process of the utilization of assistance by the Most institution. The Committee
would also like to be informed whether any Audit has been undertaken of the Institutions that received
assistance under the NMCP . (Para 103)
Action Taken
Under the Scheme 'Support for Entrepreneurial and Managerial Development of SMEs through
Incubators', 440 innovative ideas were approved in the Twelfth Five Year Plan up to 31.3.2017. The main
objective of the scheme is to promote emerging technological and knowledge-based innovative ventures that
seek the nurturing of ideas from innovators, beyond the traditional activities of Micro, Small & Medium
Enterprises (MSMEs). The scheme is implemented through duly approved Host institutes / Business Incubators
(HI/BI). The purpose of the small dose of assistance provided under the present scheme is to support
students / ex-students of science and technology and entrepreneurs to try out their innovative ideas (in
processes and products) at the laboratory or workshop stage and beyond (to the extent possible) -to carry
forward the idea from its mere conception to 'know-how' and then to 'do how' stage. It may thus be seen
that the scheme is designed for sustaining, at some basic or introductory level, the incubation of ideas that
would have otherwise been lost for want of support.
The guidelines do provide for situations where many Host Institutions, where other similar programmes
for enriching and incubating innovations are already on, this assistance could be dovetailed within them, by
way of an additional encouragement / sustenance, without leading to duplication or unnecessary double
benefits.
Monitoring is accomplished through reviewing progress reports from His, and release of subsequent
installment. It is for Host Institution or its BI to benchmark the expectations from its students and
entrepreneurs (and their ideas) at the level that is considered appropriate and to provide the level of assistance
that is actually required to operationalise ideas.
The financial sanction orders issued to the approved HI/BIs, whose proposed ideas/concepts have
been duly approved, will be officially informed that the expenditure incurred against sanctioned funds will be
open to inspection by the sanctioning authority, CAG, CCA in the MoMSME. Copies of the said sanction
orders are also sent to the Principal Director of Audit, Economic & Service Ministry, New Delhi. However
this office has no any formal method of auditing the HI/BI.

This was reduced to ` l082.90 cr. at RE stage. An unspent balance of `343 cr. alongwith `70 cr. towards
interest earned and margin money refunded were already available with KVIC. Whole of the allocation of

was been put into operation w.e.f. 1st July, 2016. The system was new and initially taking lot of time by the
agencies to operate the same. In addition, during the FY 2016-17, beside the cases applied on the on-line
system, there were lot of old cases already sanctioned by the Banks off-line. All the nodal banks accounts

on 31.03.2016, which would be disbursed during the current year 2017-18. During the current year

If wages are to be determined on piece rate basis, then steps must be taken to improve productivity of
artisans without drudgery. KVIC must ensure production and supply of solar charkhas at reasonable rate

60
and any other improved version that enhances productivity, for which the Khadi and VI Grant for S&T may
be increased provided its utilization too is improved. (Para 180)
Action Taken
Welfare of Khadi artisans is primary objective of KVIC and all the policies of KVIC revolved around
improving their welfare and reduction of their drudgery. KVIC has periodically under taken various S&T
projects aiming at increasing their wages, production and productivity. Further KVIC has launched Solar
Charkha on trial basis and based on the outcome it will be taken on large scale.
Ministry of MSME and KVIC has emphasized for development and implementation of Solar Charkha in
the field to get more productivity as well as higher wages to the artisans. Keeping in view the importance
KVIC is taking all possible steps to extend the financial support for new Research and Development proposals
under development of solar power operated charkhas in different spindles.
However, the Khadi Gramodyog Sansthan, Ahmedabad vide their report has informed that the production
of hanks has been increased to 2.5 to 3 folds on the newly developed 12 spindle high speed amber charkha
running with solar energy i.e. 80 to 100 hanks from average of 35 hanks. Further, it has reported that the
wages has increased to four fold from an average earning of ` 100/- to ` 400/-.
KVIC has sanctioned following 5 R&D projects under solar charkha to strengthen the KVI sector in
terms of productivity as well as higher earnings to the artisans:
i. Design and development of 12 spindle high speed amber charkha running with solar energy
ii. Design and development of 08 spindle high speed amber charkha suitable for manufacturing
coarse yarn spun from very short staple length of Desi fibres.
iii. Field Trials/dissemination of 10 spindle solar charkha and solar looms technology
iv. Energy audit for solar charkhas Field trials of 16 spindle solar power driven charkha.

Action Taken
Khadi Mark Regulation 2013 came into existence on 19th July 2013 which applies to persons who are
engaged in the production, sale or trading of Khadi and Khadi products or who are desirous of producing,

61
selling or trading in Khadi and Khadi products and to certified Khadi Institutions (KIs) who hold a valid

Hence, it is mandatory for every person to obtain Khadi Mark Certificate who is engaged or desirous of
producing, selling or trading in Khadi and Khadi Products.

The Grievance Cell has been constituted in the O/o AS&DC, MSME as per the para 13 of the PP Policy
which clearly points out that a Grievance Cell is to be set up in the Ministry of MSME and that Cell will take
up the issues raised by the MSE with the concerned procuring agencies. Ministry of MSME has already
requested the procuring agencies for nominating Nodal Officer responsible for implementation of the PP
Policy in their organization.
Recommendation/Observation
The Committee desires that the details of Prabhat Kumar Committee and its financial and legislative
implications may be informed to the Committee. The Committee may also be apprised if the Ministry has set

63
milestones for rolling out the Policy provisions in short and medium terms and benchmarks to assess the
success of Policy. (Para 260)
Action Taken
The Ministry of MSME, in December 2015, constituted Prabhat Kumar Committee to make
recommendations towards a national policy for MSMEs. The Committee has submitted its report to the
Ministry in January 2017 which is under examination. The Report is available on official website dcmsme.gov.in/
under this link http://dcmsme.gov.in/LegalFramework.htm
Recommendation/Observation
The MSME sector which is critical for the equitable growth and employment and entrepreneurship in
the economy, is a fact that can hardly be overstated. Though the Budget allocation for the Ministry of
MSME is not proportionate to the importance of this Sector, the Committee reiterates that the available
resources need to be used efficiently for the targeted objectives. The Committee has often noted the excuse of
Schemes being demand-driven for the under-utilization of allocations. If the Ministry is not convinced of
demand, then it should not seek allocation. The Ministry has not been able to generate demand for its
Schemes in a Sector which is wide spread over several sectors and is starved of any worthwhile policy
intervention. With number of KIs reducing and low employability of training courses the Committee wonders
the quality of monitoring at Ministry's level and efficacy of its institutional network in States and at grass
root levels. (Para 268)
Action Taken
The increase in Khadi Institutions (KIs) has registered a numerical increase but not in geometrical
ratio. However, KVIC has taken a policy initiative to bring is more KIs by opening the door for individuals,
partnership firms and companies and they can submit their application online and the process of registration
of certificate has been simplified, time-bound and online process.
KVIC through its Departmental and Non-Departmental Training centres conduct awareness programmes
throughout the country to propagate various schemes courses. Also the e-learning module have been uploaded
on web portal of KVIC in order to facilitate reach the un-employed youths. A call centre have been set up in
order to take a stock of candidates trained in Khadi and V.I. Sector and also to provide necessary guidance
about the schemes of KVIC to the beneficiary.
Recommendation/Observation
In view of CAG's repeated adverse observation of Ministry of MSME, the Committee has been asking
for Performance Audit of major Schemes by CAG and not the third party evaluation. The Committee may be
apprised of the outcome of the CAG's audit and its compliance. The Committee also recommends that Audit
Paras must be appropriately included in the Annual Report of the Ministry. (Para 274)
Action Taken
Ministry has taken up the issue of Performance Audit of all schemes. A request has been made vide
letter No. 3(1)/2016-EDI dated 16.12.2016 to CAG to undertake performance audit of the ATI Scheme as
per the recommendation of the Committee. Reply from CAG Headquarter is awaited.

64
O/o DC (MSME) has written a letter dated 09.05.2016 to CAG requesting them to conduct the
Performance Audit of 18 Tool Rooms & Technology Development Centres, under Audit Regulations 2007
(Chapter 7) of CAG Act, 1971. A team of Officers from CAG Office, New Delhi has visited this office in
Sep. 2016 and asked to provide various documents pertaining to Tool Rooms. All the documents have been
provided to them. Response from CAG is awaited. Further, O/o DC (MSME) has also written a letter dated
15.02.2017 to CAG requesting them to conduct Performance Audit of other major schemes of this Office.
Performance audit/evaluation study of PMEGP scheme has already been undertaken in the current
financial year. In the Annual Report of the Ministry for the year 2016-17, Audit Para No. 12.1 of Report No.
11 of 2016 has been shown under pending C&AG Audit Paras. However, the reply of this Audit Paragraph
has been uploaded on the Audit Para Monitoring System (APMS) web portal.

INTRODUCTION
I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Industry, having
been authorized by the Committee, hereby present this Two Hundred Eighty-Fifth Report on Action
Taken Notes furnished by the Department of Heavy Industry (Ministry of Heavy Industries and Public
Enterprises) on the recommendations contained in the Committee's Two Hundred Eighty-First Report on
the Demands For Grants (2017-18) pertaining to Department of Heavy Industry.
2. I, thank the Department of Heavy Industry (Ministry of Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises)
for furnishing the Action Taken Notes on the recommendations contained in the Committee's Two
Hundred Eighty-First Report.

  N EW D ELHI; RAM CHANDRA PRASAD SINGH
15th November, 2017 Chairman,
Kartik 15, 1939  (Saka) Department-related Parliamentary Standing
Committee on Industry
Rajya Sabha

REPORT
The Action Taken Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Ministry of Heavy
Industries and Public Enterprises (Department of Heavy Industry) on the recommendations contained in the
Committee's Two Hundred and Eighty-first Report on the Demands for Grants (2017-18) pertaining to
Department of Heavy Industry.
2. Action Taken Notes received from the Ministry of Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises (Department
of Heavy Industry) in respect of the recommendations contained in the 281st Report have been categorized
as follows:
Chapter-I The recommendations/observations, which have been accepted by the Ministry.
The Committee notes that the Ministry has accepted its recommendations as mentioned
in the Chapter - I of the Report.
Chapter-II The recommendations/observations which the Committee does not desire to pursue
further in view of the Government's replies.
In respect of these recommendations, the Committee is convinced with the logic and
explanations advanced by the Ministry and therefore does not want to pursue them
further for the present.
Chapter-III The recommendations/observations in respect of which the Committee has not accepted
replies of the Ministry and desires the Ministry to review their replies.
The Committee is not convinced with the replies of the Ministry in respect of
recommendations contained in Chapter - III and desires that the Ministry in the light of
further recommendations/observations of the Committee furnish explanations thereof.
Chapter-IV The recommendations/observations in respect of which the Committee desire further
comments of the Ministry.
In respect of recommendations placed in Chapter-IV, the Ministry has either furnished the interim
replies; therefore, the Committee desires that the Ministry may furnish Action Taken Notes in respect
of recommendations categorized in Chapter-IV in detail and to the point, as per the intention and spirit
of the recommendations of the Committee.
3. The details of the action taken replies of the Ministry and recommendations/observations of
the Committee thereon are given in the succeeding pages.

2
CHAPTER-I
THE RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS WHICH HA VE BEEN
ACCEPTED BY THE MINISTRY
Recommendation/Observation
In tune with the Vision and Mission of the Department, the Committee observes that schemes such
as 'Enhancement of Competitiveness in Capital Goods Sector' and F AME- India have been launched and
are being nurtured carefully by DHI to facilitate the Heavy Industry sector. However, coming to the
portion of Vision and Mission relating to CPSEs, the Committee finds that there is a lot of lost ground
that is to be made up by the Department. The fact that the growth of Bharat Heavy Electricals Ltd
(BHEL) finds specific mention in the Mission statement underlines the crucial nature of the prospects
of the Company to the economic interest of the nation. In this context, the Committee observes that by
making growth of BHEL an integral of its Mission, the Department has entrusted upon itself the
responsibilities of ensuring efficient performance of its flagship company. (Para 8)
Action Taken
Factual Observation of the Committee noted by DHL
Recommendation/ observation
The Committee observes that during the XII Plan period, the Budget Estimate (BE) of the Department
has mostly seen reductions under Plan Head at the Revised Estimate (RE) stage. Even so, it is encouraging
that the Department has been able to utilize its RE amount to the maximum during the Plan period. Over
the years, the Committee has noticed delays in approvals as reason for many schemes/projects not getting
operationalized on time resulting in scaling down of allocations at RE stage. From the ensuing year, the
Committee expects this glitch to be removed and the Department finding it easier to spread its expenditure
more evenly considering that the presentation of the Budget has been advanced by the Government to
ensure that funds are made available to the Ministries/ Departments right from beginning of the Financial
Year. (Para 11)
Action Taken
During the XII Plan period, the Budget provision was kept for the years 2012-13, 2013-14 and
2014-15 for the scheme on Enhancement of Competitiveness in the Indian Capital Goods Sector. However,
it was reduced to zero at RE stage because there was delay for the approval of scheme by CCEA as
the said scheme was approved only on 15.09.2014 and was notified 05.11.2014. Similarly, another
scheme/R&D project for Development of Advanced Ultra Supercritical (AUSC) Technology for Thermal
Power Plants was approved by the Cabinet only on 10.08.2016 and therefore the Budget allocation made
for the years 2014-15 and 2015-16 was reduced to zero at RE stage.
Moreover, Department has been able to make optimum utilization of the funds at RE stage. The
observation of the DRPSC has been noted for compliance.
Recommendation/observation
While assessing the AE for 2016-17, as available during mid- February, 2017, the Committee notes
that 
` 942.62 cr remains to be utilized yet during the month and a half left in the year. It is expected
2

3
that this amount will be utilized completely without any constraints that can be posed by the provisions
of the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act. (Para 24)
Action Taken
By the end of month February an amount of ` 2404.76 crore was utilized. An amount of ` 400
crore for providing interest free Non-Plan loan for payment of salary/statuary dues, Bank Borrowing,
TDS, LIC dues, EDLI, Sales Tax, Service Tax, VAT etc and VRS/VSS compensation on account of
proposed closure of Instrumentation Ltd. Kota (ILK) as per Cabinet Decision dated 30.11.2016 was
approved in the 3rd and final batch of Supplementary demand for Grants 2016-17. However, almost
whole RE amount were exhausted by the March end 2017.
Recommendation/Observation
The Committee notes that NATRIP has received yet another extension from the CCEA on account
of forex variation, statutory levies, rise in input cost and other factors like change in scope of supply.
The project, originally intended to be completed by April 2011 at the cost of ` 1718.cr , has now got a
revised cost of ` 3727 cr and an expected completion by July, 2019. According to the Department, the
latest extension and revised cost approvals by the Union Cabinet has brought the NATRIP project on
track. The Committee derives confidence from the said submission of the Department and expects that
NATRIP will finally be completed by July, 2019 and no further extensions or cost over runs will happen.
Meanwhile, the Committee also takes note of the fact that the contributions of NATRIP can result in
the scaling up of automobile exports from India, giving impetus to the "Make in India" program and
also meet certification needs of Indian automotive industry. (Para 33)
Action Taken
All efforts will be made to ensure that further time and cost overrunning in the project do not recur.
Recommendation/observation
The Committee finds that for 2017-18, FAME-India scheme has attracted an increase in allocation
of 
` 52.1 cr compared to the previous year and takes into account the submission of the Department that
this amount will be utilized fully. It is an appreciative fact that the restriction of the scheme to limited
cities for two and three-wheelers has been proposed to be lifted in the modified scheme. It is felt that
this lifting of restriction may be appropriately considered for other type of vehicles as well, further, the
Committee finds that the deliverables for 2017-18 under the scheme include subsiding 1.5 lakh vehicles.
It is understood that this subsidy is currently released to the Registered Automobile Manufacturers
(OEMs) for the sale of electric/hybrid vehicles. In this regard, the Committee wants the Department to
examine the feasibility of transferring the subsidy component to individual buyers rather than the
Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs). This will help increase the visibility of the scheme much
more besides the other advantages related to the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mode. The Committee
also feels that DHI should consider popularising the scheme more extensively through visual and print
media. (Para 38)
Action Taken
Out of the fund @ ` 175 crore allocated for FAME India Scheme for the F.Y. 2017-18, an amount
of ` 70.25 crore has already been sanctioned/released in the 1st Quarter of the year i.e. during April-
June, 2017. Hence, it is apparent that the allocated fund will be utilized fully.

4
It may be clarified that the scheme was made applicable for the sale of Electric and Hybrid 2 (Two)
Wheelers and 3 (Three) Wheelers anywhere in India, without any geographical limitations vide Gazette
Notification S.O. 2696(E) dated 30th September 2015.
Para no. 11 of the FAME India Scheme Guidelines provides that based on the outcome and
experience gained in the Phase-1, the scheme shall be reviewed appropriately with inputs from stakeholders
and shall be considered for implementation post 31st March 2017, with appropriate allocation of funds
in the future. It may, however, be informed that the Phase-1 of the scheme, which was upto 31st March
2017, has been extended for a further period of six months i.e. upto 30th September 2017 vide Gazette
Notification S.O. No. 1055(E) dated 30th March 2017. Accordingly the scheme is being reviewed for
finalizing phase-II of the scheme.
Under Demand Incentive Delivery Mechanism of the scheme, the beneficiary got the incentive
immediately at the time of purchase of electric/hybrid vehicle from the dealer. The dealer through
respective OEMs got reimbursement from the Government under this scheme. However, the dealer has
to get the certificate from beneficiary under his/her signature uploaded in the online portal of the
Government, which clearly mentions that he/she has got incentive for the prescribed amount under
FAME India Scheme of the Government of India. However, the Government has already made Aadhar
Number for individual beneficiary mandatory to avail the benefit of demand incentive. This online system
for extending demand incentive to beneficiary under the scheme has also been appreciated by the DBT
Mission Team visited this Department. Hence, there seems to be clear visibility of the scheme apart from
immediate realization of monetary benefit by the beneficiary under the scheme.
The valuable suggestion given by the Hon'ble Committee for popularizing the scheme through visual
and print media is noted for compliance in future.
Recommendation/observation
Considering this, the Committee is of the opinion that the onus of avoiding the receipts of such
proposals lies with DHI/DCAAI. Accordingly, it is felt that DCCAI should come out with clear guidelines
for submitting the R&D proposals to act as a reliable reference document for people to prepare the said
proposals. The parameters on which proposals have already been approved by DCAAI may also be made
available to the aspiring proposers and may be given wider publicity. All such activities may be
coordinated under a helpdesk or some such similar arrangement. Further, the Committee recommends that
urgent action may be taken to improve fund utilization under DCAAI as it administrates the Auto Cess
collected by the Government to be used specifically for the betterment of the very important Automotive
Sector . (Para 44)
Action Taken
Cess on sale of automobiles is levied as per notification issued in 1983 @ 1/8th of one percent in
terms of the Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951. For sake of administrative convenience
this Cess is collected along with excise duty collections but is maintained in a separate head of account.
This money is being used by Development Council for Automotive and Allied Industries that is chaired
by Secretary, DHI to fund pre-competitive R&D projects for the benefit of the industry through a
transparent process of Cess Committee which is chaired by Secretary, DHI. The proposals sent are

5
evaluated by a Screening Committee and Technical Sub-committee in the light of the Draft guidelines for
submitting R&D project mentioned below:-
Guideline for Submitting R&D Projects under Cess Fund
1. Name of the project
2. Name of the Institution/Agency executing the project
3. Need & Justification of the project
4. Targeted beneficiary
5. Whether similar Research work undertaken earlier; if so the detail thereof and the reason for
undertaking this project.
6. Relevance to Automobile Industry
7. Total Cost of the project
8. Duration of the project
9. Present capacity of the Institution/agency to take up this project
10. Whether the project has been approved by the concerned governing body of the Institution/Agency.
However, recommendations of the Hon'ble Committee have been noted for compliance.
Recommendation/ observation
The Committee takes note of the fact that the areas that were not covered under the Scheme for
Enhancement of Competitiveness in the Indian Capital Goods Sector are being addressed under the
proposed expanded scheme in tune with the National Capital Goods Policy, 2016. It is also taken note
that the Department had sought an allocation of 
` 255.45 cr for 2017-18 to fund sub-schemes under
the Policy. However, the actual allocation under BE has only been ` 150.00 cr which is still more than
double the funds provided last year. The Committee observes that the Ministry of Finance could be
pursued in this regard and when as more sub-schemes under the policy matures as the year progresses and
funds could again be sought at the RE stage . (Para 54)
Action Taken
At the time of preparing B.E 2017-18 an Expenditure of ` 150.00 crore was projected on basis of
projects already approved under different component of the on-going CG Scheme. However, there is a
likelihood of approval of proposals from IIT Delhi and IIT Kharagpur which may result in requirement
of further Budgetary allocation.
Apart of the above under the National Capital Goods Policy, Subs-Schemes are being formulated
for which additional fund will be required.
Based on the requirement further fund for Capital Goods Sector will be sought at R.E. Stage
Recommendation/observation
The Committee finds it encouraging to note that the Advanced Ultra Super-Critical (AUSC) Technology
project has finally got the approval to operationalize. It is extremely appreciative that the project has

6
been approved to be executed in Mission Mode and a component-wise timeline has also been set. Cost
overruns, if any, are to be funded by the stakeholders. All this makes the Project a game changer in terms
of efficient project structuring and orchestration. A timely completion should be a reasonable expectation
and would wipe out the history of frustrating delay that normally occurs during the process of securing
the necessary approvals for the projects. The Committee comprehends that successful completion of the
project would propel the country to the primary position among leading countries of the world who are
competing to master this cutting-edge technology that would reduce coal consumption and carbon dioxide
pollution, phenomenally. (Para 60)
Action Taken
The observations of the Committee are noted. BHEL on its part has initiated work on the R&D phase
of the project in a mission mode and all efforts are being and will be made for its timely completion
within the envisaged schedule.
Recommendation/Observation
The Committee notes that the NITI Aayog has reviewed and provided its recommendations on 24
CPSEs under DHL Out of the 25 operational CPSEs under DHI, besides the ones marked for closure,
5 have been recommended for strategic disinvestment, 4 for transfer to State Governments, one for part
disinvestment and 2 to be considered later for disinvestment. Only HMT Machine Tools has been
recommended for revival. The Committee observes that if these recommendations are approved, DHI will
be left with very few CPSEs under its administrative control. (Para 64)
Action Taken
NITI Aayog was entrusted the responsibility to critically review the performance of CPSEs and give
their recommendations on their future. They have recommended closure of some chronically sick CPSEs
under DHI and transfer of some to the State Govt. They have also recommended strategic disinvestment,
merger of some profit making CPSEs. However, the final decision on closure or disinvestment is taken
by the Cabinet/CCEA after detailed study and due consultations with Ministries / Departments concerned
in the larger public interest.
It is correct that with the closure of a number of CPSEs, DHI will be left with only a few. However,
this will provide an opportunity to the Department to focus more on the well performing CPSEs viz.
BHEL to enhance their performance further. Keeping in view the future scenario in the power sector, an
ambitious R&D project with a capital outlay of ` 1554 crore has been embarked upon for development
of Advanced Ultra Super Critical (AUSC) technology for 'thermal power plants which will reduce the
carbon emission and increase the efficiency of thermal power plants in future. This project is undertaken
by a consortium led by BHEL with NTPC, IGCAR and DST.
DHI has a much larger role to play for industrial and economic development of the country. It has
been entrusted to steer the Capital Goods Sector to become a driver of growth in the emerging industrial
scenario. Government, of India/ DHI has launched the National Capital Goods Policy and has also
introduced several schemes to promote technological and engineering innovations in the field of Capital
Goods sector. There is a great potential in this field and a lot of work is required to be done.
Apart from the above, DHI is also responsible for framing and implementing policy for Automobile
sector. A lot is being done for making India an International manufacturing hub for Automobiles and

7
Automobile components. Government of India / DHI has launched the Faster Adoption and Manufacturing
of (Hybrid &) Electric Vehicles in India (FAME- INDIA) Scheme to support the hybrid/electric vehicle
market Development and its manufacturing eco-system to achieve self-sustenance. This Scheme would
provide" affordable and environmentally friendly public and private transportation/vehicular mobility options
for the masses, further, a project namely National Automotive Testing and R&D Infrastructure Project
(NATRIP) is also being implemented under DHI which envisages setting up of world class automotive
testing and homologation facilities in India.
DHI will be focusing on both of these champion Sectors.
Recommendation/Observation
The Committee takes into cognizance the fact that the efforts taken by BHEL to arrest the downward
spiral of the Company during the last few years has begun to bear fruit. This is evident from the fact
that both the production performance and the Profit before Tax" (PBT) of the Company is anticipated
to pick up from 2016-17 onwards. Considering the elongated cycle of capital goods market, the Committee
expects the upward swing in the performance of BHEL to be gradual and anticipated to be facilitated
by the impetus of the Government to invest more in power and related infrastructure in coming times.
The Committee observes that the success of BHEL in power plant commissioning and in order booking
indicates that the path of revival for the Company lies largely in focusing on strengthening their core
business. (Para 75)
Action Taken
The Government of India has taken various initiatives for the development, improvement and
resolving issues affecting the power sector - which has been the main line of business of BHEL.
However, the Draft National Electricity Plan (NEP) released recently (in December 2016) by the Central
Electricity Authority (CEA) indicates conservative projections for coal based thermal power plants.
With a view to have a broader business and product offering - including in the power segment, as
well as address any contingency particularly against the backdrop of dampened new capacity addition
scenario (projected by CEA) in the conventional power generation sector going forward, BHEL has been
and is also continuously exploring options and making careful diversification efforts. Such efforts include
in areas such as Renewable Energy, Power Transmission, Water business, Transportation, Defence etc.
Recommendation/Observation
The Committee also notes that the Department have issued necessary instructions to the HPC to put
up their procurement policy for bamboo on the website to bring more transparency. (Para 92)
Action Taken
The revised and updated bamboo procurement policy has been uploaded on the Website so as to
further ensure transparency in bamboo procurement.

8
CHAPTER-II
THE RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH THE COMMITTEE DOES NOT DESIRE
TO PURSUE FURTHER IN VIEW OF THE GOVERNMENT'S REPLIES
Recommendation/Observation
The Committee takes note that the Department has quoted varying figures in its Annual Report
regarding the number of CPSEs under it. While 31 CPSEs are under the 'administrative oversight' of
DHI, the number of 'operative CPSEs' under it stands at 25. The Committee assumes that this variance
in figures is consequent to the closure of certain CPSEs during the preceding year. However, while
perusing the status of CPSEs as recommended by NITI Aayog placed at Annexure II of the Annual Report
(2016-17), the number of CPSEs recommended for closure is 7. If this figure is to be considered, the
number of 'operating CPSEs' should be 24. The Committee observes this as a divergence which should
have been avoided by more specific description of the status of CPSEs under DHI, elucidating the
rationale adopted for the same. Accordingly, the Committee recommends that the Department should
ensure that important documents like the Annual Report should be spelt out unambiguously and without

Action Taken Replies
R&D represents a journey from mind to market. Further, progressive technological changes require
carrying out R&D activities on a continuous basis so as to provide belter or more efficient products,
services and solutions. In India, getting advanced technologies nowadays from outside is generally an
expensive and time-consuming affair, besides it does not inculcate self-reliance. It is therefore crucial to
incentivise companies and organisations taking risks by investing in R&D, which can lead to development
of indigenous technology and new products for benefiting the society. In this regard, Section 35 (2AB)
of Income Tax Act, 1961 provided for weighted deduction of 200% of the expenditure incurred by a
Company on scientific research on an approved in-house research and development facility from financial
year 2010-11 to 2016-17. This also facilitated promotion of R&D efforts in the Country, and has also
been an inducement for investing in in-house R&D activities by many companies/organisations. However,
the Finance Act 2016 amended the aforesaid section and reduced the weighted deduction from 200% to
150% from financial year 2017-18 to 2019-20, and also further restricted this to 100% from 01.04.2020.
The reduction in weighted deduction affects the income tax liability of many companies engaged in R&D
and innovation, including BHEL which is among the highest R&D spenders in the Country in the
engineering and manufacturing segment. Given the importance of R&D for any economy, it is important
for the Government of India to expand incentives so as to encourage companies and organisations to
carry out or expand R&D activity and also contributing to innovation in the Country. Hence, the
allowability of weighted deduction under section 35(2AB) of Income Tax Act should be restored to 200%
by the Govt. of India, as was available earlier. This will also facilitate companies and organisations in
contributing to the ecosystem of "Make in India" programme.
